Ministers to drop foie gras imports ban to help seal EU food trade deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Animal welfare charities criticise ‘backwards step’ on foie gras, production of which has been banned in UK since 2007.
  • Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week.
  • As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government confirms its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Animal welfare charities criticise ‘backwards step’ on foie gras, production of which has been banned in UK since 2007.

Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week.

As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government confirms its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc.

Industry observers note that labour promised before coming to power that it would ban foie gras imports. Before the election, Steve Reed, the then shadow environment secretary, said Labour would “ban the commercial import of foie gras, where ducks and geese are aggressively force-fed”. He labelled the practice “beyond disgusting”.

Foie gras is made by force-feeding ducks and geese grain through a funnel or tube that has been thrust down the bird’s neck – a process known as gavage that swells the animal’s liver to many times its normal size. The livers are then harvested.

It has been revealed that banning it has proved difficult as EU countries including France produce and export the product and are against other members putting in place an import ban. The Guardian reported earlier this year that ministers were preparing to drop the ban in order to secure concessions.

It has been revealed that sustainability chefs and animal welfare charities have criticised the U-turn. Boris Johnson’s government promised to use the powers granted by Brexit to ban the “cruel” product, which still appears on menus across the country almost seven years after the UK officially left the EU.

Some restaurants still sell foie gras but many shops have removed it from sale, including the king’s grocer, Fortnum & Mason, which took it off shelves in 2021. The production of foie gras has been banned in the UK since 2007.

Recent findings suggest that the French chef Alexis Gauthier used to sell more foie gras than any other restaurant in London before converting to a vegan diet and menu. He now sells a mushroom-based “faux gras” to customers of his Soho restaurant, who include the former Beatle Paul McCartney. Gauthier said the ban being dropped was “terrible news”.

“I find it very sad our government capitulates so easily,” he said. “The cruelty of foie gras belongs firmly in the history books, not in a progressive society in 2026.”.

In a recent development, will Murray, a co-founder of the sustainable British restaurant Fallow, also based in London, serves a mushroom parfait rather than foie gras. He remarked: “This feels like a step in the wrong direction with regards to animal welfare. I think London diners aren’t really asking for a significant return of foie gras on menus.”.

David Bowles, the head of public affairs at the RSPCA, mentioned: “We are extremely disappointed that farm animal welfare laws have been put on the chopping block as part of this fresh deal. Any suggestions prepares to act on foie gras are being shelved to ease EU realignment are deeply concerning for animals and would be a clear backwards step.”.

A spokesperson for the charity Four Paws noted: “The UK prohibited the production of foie gras nearly 20 years ago because of the serious animal welfare concerns associated with force-feeding ducks and geese. Yet foie gras produced using these same methods can still be imported and sold here. As the UK strengthens its relationship with the EU, animal welfare must not become a casualty of closer trade ties.”.

Government insiders indicated that the ban would be dropped but noted that the method of production was banned in the UK. A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs mentioned the method raises welfare concerns.

They mentioned: “We are negotiating a food and drink deal that will slash red tape and costly paperwork, make it easier and cheaper to export seafood, boost the British economy by up to £5bn a year, and back British businesses and jobs. We are working closely with businesses to ensure a smooth transition so they can make the most of the benefits this deal unlocks.”.

US and Mexico lose measles-free status

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the ​United States is experiencing its highest number ​of cases in more than three decades.
  • Industry observers note that as ​of November 12, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have confirmed 5,412 measles cases and 6 deaths.
  • Pennsylvania has been the worst-hit state, reporting seven measles-related deaths and more than 1,500 cases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the ​United States is experiencing its highest number ​of cases in more than three decades. Some 7,700 people in the country have been infected and 13 have died since 2025.

Industry observers note that as ​of November 12, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have confirmed 5,412 measles cases and 6 deaths. US states have reported a total of 10 deaths from the highly contagious virus this year.

Pennsylvania has been the worst-hit state, reporting seven measles-related deaths and more than 1,500 cases.

Tuesday's declaration by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has few practical implications and is largely symbolic, but is the latest sign of measles' avoidable resurgence.

"Losing measles elimination status is much more than losing a public health designation. It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period, putting families and communities at risk of preventable illness, hospitalization and death," PAHO Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa said.

Thanks to a series of functioning vaccines, measles had been virtually eradicated throughout most of the developed world for decades.

Vaccine hesitancy and disinformation has risen in recent years in the US, seemingly fueled at least in part by the COVID pandemic.

According to recent reports, the rising influence of renowned vaccine critic Robert F. Kennedy Jr., now the US Health Secretary — who dropped out of the 2024 presidential election campaign to form an alliance with Donald Trump — was one of the clearest indicators of this.

According to recent reports, "This is a serious warning for our region, but it is not an irreversible setback," PAHO Director Barbosa said. "We know how to prevent measles, and we know how to stop its transmission. With sustained commitment to vaccination, strong surveillance and effective outbreak response, the Americas can eliminate measles transmission once again.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

As of November 13, PAHO stated that the Americas region had reported 58,213 measles cases and 82 deaths, compared with 12,806 cases during the same period last year.

The organization considers endemic transmission to be re-established when the same measles virus genotype and lineage circulate uninterrupted for 12 months or more in a country.

Canada had reached this status in November 2025, with Bolivia, Mexico and the US now deemed to have joined it.

The PAHO remarked that Canda had "interrupted the chain of transmission" that led to its designation and was working to regain elimination status.

Meanwhile, it remarked the other three countries "are implementing measures to strengthen vaccination, surveillance and outbreak response.".

One strange Voyager 1 mystery persists as it moves beyond a light-day

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA's Voyager 1 is tracking a deep-space mystery that has stumped scientists for the past six years.
  • Industry observers note that in 2020, about eight years after leaving the solar system, the spacecraft flew into a region where the magnetic field rose like an incoming tide.
  • The sun constantly streams out charged gas and magnetism, called solar wind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA's Voyager 1 is tracking a deep-space mystery that has stumped scientists for the past six years.

Industry observers note that in 2020, about eight years after leaving the solar system, the spacecraft flew into a region where the magnetic field rose like an incoming tide. Earlier events had spiked and then faded, like waves breaking on a beach. But this tide never went out. Even today, it still hasn't receded.

The sun constantly streams out charged gas and magnetism, called solar wind. That stream blows a giant bubble around the solar system, which scientists refer to as the heliosphere. Voyager 1 exited the bubble in 2012, and its twin, Voyager 2, taking a different route, left in 2018. Both now travel through interstellar space, the thin mix of gas, magnetism, and fast-moving particles between star systems.

Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977, will reach one light-day, the distance light travels in 24 hours, or about 16 billion miles, on Wednesday, Nov. 18. That historic milestone makes the aging probe irreplaceable. No other spacecraft has explored this far beyond the sun's bubble. Every reading Voyager 1 sends home adds to the only direct measurements anyone has of the space environment between the sun and other stars.

In a recent development, that data has already taught scientists something fundamental about our home in space. Once outside the bubble, the Voyagers recorded a sharp jump in cosmic rays, the high-speed particles that supernova explosions fling across the galaxy. The readings showed that the bubble blocks roughly 75 to 85 percent of that radiation, depending on how active the sun is.

Recent findings suggest that "We see how much the sun and this astrosphere all around us, known as the heliosphere, protects us," noted Jamie Rankin, Voyager's deputy project scientist and a research scholar at Princeton University, during a NASA webinar last November. "It's pretty incredible, and it's a good question to ask: Without our heliosphere, would life exist?".

Beyond the bubble, Voyager 1 found four bumps in the magnetic field between 2012 and 2020. The magnetic field is the invisible magnetism that fills space. A 2021 study, published in The Astrophysical Journal, identified two of the bumps as sharp shock waves, a bit like sonic booms. The other two were gentler, broader swells that scientists call pressure fronts.

In a recent development, the earlier pressure front in 2016 took about 400 days to die down. But the latest swell, known as "pressure front 2," is still going. Voyager 1 hit it in when it was about 149 times farther from the sun than Earth. In just eight days, the magnetic field increased by about one-third. That continues to be the strangest thing Voyager 1 has seen beyond the bubble, Rankin indicates.

Effects from the sun usually die out within a few months, Linda Spilker, Voyager's project scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, told Mashable.

"It might be an effect coming from interstellar space," Spilker noted in an email. "Voyager 1 continues to observe this phenomenon, and scientists hope to see what happens if it ends, one good reason to keep Voyager 1 flying.".

Recent findings suggest that computer simulations offer little help for solving the mystery. The 2021 study found that none of the leading models could reproduce the mix of shocks, swells, and placid stretches that Voyager 1 encountered.

It has been revealed that figuring it out could show how far the sun's influence truly extends, even outside the bubble. The 2021 study traced the earlier events to ripples that form when big bursts from the sun slam into the edge of the heliosphere and then roll outward.

Sources indicate that but the clock is ticking. Each Voyager runs on a nuclear battery that loses about 4 watts of power a year. That has forced the team to switch off some instruments in order to conserve energy. The spacecraft still run instruments that measure magnetism, radio signals, and cosmic rays. Scientists need those tools to keep monitoring the pressure front.

If Voyager 1 holds on long enough, it may see how and where the mysterious pressure front ends.

"For a while, it was kind of unknown what would the Voyagers be doing after they turned off their cameras, because that was kind of like the end of the planetary science phase of the mission," Rankin noted. "But it turned out that the original people operating the spacecraft, they were visionaries, and they wanted to see where these boundaries lie.".

Industry News: Nike lays out financial goals ahead of first investor day in 9 years

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nike said Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.
  • The retailer also laid out a financial framework and said that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50.
  • Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nike said Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.

The retailer also laid out a financial framework and said that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50. The company said higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements would help it reach its goals.

Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35.

The organization also introduced a strategy it's calling Full Stride Ahead, which the company said aims "to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth.".

Nike CEO Elliott Hill told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the fresh initiative is about "being closer to the athletes we serve.".

"What's different today is the depth and breadth we're taking from an innovation perspective," Hill said.

Recent findings suggest that he added that Nike is emphasizing sportswear at a time when sports have never been more relevant around the world. Hill also mentioned Nike is working to regain its cultural relevance, after a perceived dropoff contributed to its slowdown both in its home market and in China.

Nike mentioned it would focus on performance sports and sportswear opportunities "with the greatest potential for long-term growth," and said its five priority sports would be running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor.

Nike is holding an investor day at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the company aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump.

Industry observers note that last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it said would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year.

Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the tech giant remarked it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the manufacturer's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike said the turnaround proposal is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031.

Nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have remarked the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers.

At the same time, Nike revealed last quarter that it's creating a new global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The manufacturer remarked it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence.

Nike COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy told CNBC the company sees an opportunity to triple its business in the country over the next five years.

He added that Nike's broader strategy will position it for success in India.

"If you look at the three components, brand building, landing those innovations into marketplaces in an increasingly locally connected fashion and then doing all of those things in a much faster pace really aligns well with the aspirations for India," he said.

Industry observers note that CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has said that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the organization elsewhere, including internationally.

The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.

Shares of Nike have fallen 50% over the past two years.

Tech Report: UK government ‘breaking the law’ by not stopping decline of wild birds

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Populations at lowest level on record with 45% of native breeding species in decline, environment regulator says.
  • Environment secretary Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the catastrophic decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has noted.
  • Newly introduced data reveals wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Populations at lowest level on record with 45% of native breeding species in decline, environment regulator says.

Environment secretary Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the catastrophic decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has noted.

Newly introduced data reveals wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.

In the last five decades, Britain has lost more than 73 million wild birds from its landscape, according to the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO).

The loss of wild birds includes some of Britain’s best-loved garden birds, including swifts, turtledoves and tree sparrows, as well as wood warblers and bullfinches.

Ministers have legal responsibilities to take action to recover bird populations to healthy levels, as well as specific duties to designate Special Protection Areas (SPAs) where birds and their habitats are legally protected.

But the Office for Environmental Protection (OEP), the independent environmental regulator, said on Wednesday that the environment secretary, her department and Natural England were all breaking the law by failing to protect wild birds.

Eagle has breached environmental law by failing to classify new SPAs, extend existing sites or add new species to those that are protected, the regulator mentioned.

Natural England is in breach of environmental law, according to the OEP, by failing to take the action needed to maintain or restore wild bird populations to appropriate levels and ensure they have sufficient habitats.

The government’s independent nature adviser is also accused of breaching the law by failing to carry out a review of whether there is sufficient habitat for wild birds.

The OEP mentioned the review was key because it was supposed to provide an expert and independent assessment of whether there is sufficient diversity and area of habitat for wild birds, as well as to identify gaps and explain what action is needed to support their recovery.

Industry observers note that the continued decline in bird populations comes despite evidence that the public’s interest and attention to wild birds is growing. In May, the RSPB reported a 47% increase in the number of people enjoying bird watching over the past eight years.

Helen Venn, chief regulatory officer for the OEP, mentioned there have been continued delays by ministers to protect bird populations.

“As a nation of bird-lovers, and with birds acting as important indicators for the state of our nature more widely, the latest statistics showing declines in the populations of some of our most treasured species are deeply concerning,” said Venn.

“This is why it is important that Defra and Natural England do carry out their legal responsibilities in a reasonable timeframe to deliver nature recovery and in relation to the classification and adaptation of SPAs on land.

“Continued delay has left a significant number of sites for wild bird populations without the levels of protection they need and allowed the scale of the actions needed to deliver a sufficient SPA network to build up.”.

There are 82 SPAs in England, as well as six cross-border and offshore sites.

The government is legally bound to expand and increase protected areas across the country as part of its 30 by 30 commitment to protect at least 30% of land and seas for nature’s recovery by 2030.

But despite repeated promises by Labour’s environment ministers, wild bird populations across the UK are showing no sign of widespread recovery, with both short and long-term trends indicating that nearly half of all species are in decline, according to Defra’s latest statistics.

Recent findings suggest that beccy Speight, the RSPB’s chief executive, said: “We now expect urgent action, including the designation of fresh and extended Special Protection Areas and other targeted measures for species such as curlew, bittern and hen harrier, which are in most need. Successive governments right across the UK have known about these problems for years. The time for navel gazing has long passed; the time for taking action is now, before it is too late.”.

The Department for Environment was approached for comment.

Republicans outspent Democrats for first time in over a decade in record 2026 midterm election political ad blitz

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Political advertisers spent a record $12.06 billion during the 2025-26 elections, making it the first time a midterm cycle outspent a presidential cycle, according to a report from advertising intelligence company AdImpact released Tuesday.
  • Total spending exceeded AdImpact's June projection by more than $460 million.
  • The elections also marked the first time in over a decade that Republicans have outspent Democrats on advertisements, according to AdImpact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Political advertisers spent a record $12.06 billion during the 2025-26 elections, making it the first time a midterm cycle outspent a presidential cycle, according to a report from advertising intelligence company AdImpact released Tuesday.

Total spending exceeded AdImpact's June projection by more than $460 million.

The elections also marked the first time in over a decade that Republicans have outspent Democrats on advertisements, according to AdImpact.

Despite Republicans leading spending, John Link, senior vice president of data at AdImpact, said that "Dems still led or were generally even with overall airings and impressions.".

In a recent development, the record spending extended across the board, with every type of race reaching a fresh high. Senate spending hit $3.39 billion, while spending on gubernatorial elections reached $2.61 billion, spending on races in the House of Representatives grew to $2.44 billion and state legislative races totaled $602 million, all records, according to AdImpact.

The 2026 midterm cycle was largely powered by megadonors, with SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk becoming the largest contributor by funneling more than $366 million into campaigns.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest donors in this year's election disproportionately favored Republicans, according to a CNBC analysis of Federal Election Commission records. Fourteen out of the 20 largest donor groups supported GOP candidates, according to that analysis.

Republicans spent $5.51 billion on political advertisements, compared with $5.11 billion spent by Democrats, according to AdImpact.

While Republican spending increased by 27% from 2024, spending by Democrats fell by 4%.

Fundraisers told CNBC in interviews that Democratic donors' hesitancy largely stems from memories of Kamala Harris' defeat in 2024, unease about the rise of democratic socialism and distrust in party leadership.

Though they were outspent, Democrats made sweeping gains against Republicans in races nationwide, taking control of both the House and the Senate and flipping seats in some of the most competitive places, including Texas and Kansas.

According to recent reports, it is not the first time spending did not align with the winners. In 2024, President Donald Trump defeated former Vice President Harris despite Democrats outspending Republicans.

While party majorities in Congress have switched hands, the most popular medium for political ads has not changed.

Broadcast television represented the largest category for spending in this year's election, accounting for 49%, or $5.85 billion, of political ad spending, according to AdImpact. Broadcast's share of political ad dollars is up slightly from 48% in 2024.

Broadcast TV's strength comes despite facing pressure from falling viewership and increasing competition from streaming.

Industry experts have told CNBC that political advertisers continue to spend on broadcast because it reaches local markets and active voting populations. The Associated Press also reported that airtime was so expensive during the midterm elections that some candidates, including Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, bought ads during national sporting events, figuring that reaching enough constituents through a national broadcast might actually be less expensive than buying across the state's local television markets.

The fastest-growing categories in this year's cycle were connected TV, or internet-connected devices like Apple TV or Roku, with $2.66 billion, and digital, with $1.91 billion. Both mediums grew double digits from the 2024 presidential election. Spending on cable and radio declined 7% and 13%, respectively, from 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I squint my eyes in confusion when Anton Osika asks if I like cakes. The CEO of Lovable was in the middle of explaining how his AI startup, flush with investment cash and recently valued at over $13 billion, is ready to shift its focus after two years. Why does the vibe-coding king care if I like sweet treats? He thinks that if I do, I might be able to vibe code a living out of that.

According to recent reports, the generative AI revolution completely flipped coding. Rather than a niche skill set where humans had to learn how to talk like computers, software development could be done by computers generating code in response to natural-language requests from humans.

Industry observers note that osika was early to this shift, launching a viral open-source tool in 2023, a precursor to Lovable. His mission? “Reduce barriers to build.” That initial spark ignited what is now one of Europe’s most dynamic startups.

Tech insiders talked nonstop last year about the transformative power of “vibe coding” that could empower anyone to build their own software. Parents could whip up custom apps to help track demanding club sports schedules. Picky eaters could create dynamic meal prepares that adapt to whatever’s in their fridge. Polyamorous people could build software to manage their relationship hierarchies. Whatever random, niche software you can imagine, you can build it.

Recent findings suggest that but Osika isn’t satisfied with helping millions of people vibe code apps for their everyday life—he also wants Lovable users to make more cash. The startup claims that around 80 percent of users arrive at the platform with a financial incentive, like building customer-facing platforms for online sales. That noted, Lovable also reports that only 35 percent currently earn revenue with their projects.

It has been revealed that that brings us back to the cake question. Lovable’s plan for next year is to help you run a small business based on your passions, like opening a cake shop. Fabian Hedin, Lovable’s other cofounder and chief technology officer, says the startup is building automations to help with everything from initial business strategy and website creation to long-term customer retention and marketing prepares.

For example, a cake shop owner receives an AI-generated morning briefing through a chatbot-style, Lovable dashboard. “You set some goals, and then the AI is proactive in helping you reach those goals,” Hedin says. This briefing analyzes the number of cake boxes sold through a holiday promotion, customer emails it automatically answered, and reminders to make financial deposits on time.

In a recent development, lovable has been a boon for savvy social media content creators, who can leverage their platforms better through vibe-coded sites. “People who have audiences themselves are building larger businesses around that,” Osika says. He recently went to a dinner in Upcoming York with creators, one of whom uses Lovable to help sell their book. Others have used it to help hawk merch.

Lovable earning the trust of burgeoning entrepreneurs is critical to the success of this upcoming endeavor, though it may be an uphill battle. Vibe-coded projects were notorious for not necessarily being secure and sometimes exposing user data.

According to recent reports, the startup was one of many vibe-coded services that came under fire this year for facilitating user-generated apps that exposed data on the open web. Earlier this month, Lovable revamped its security approach as part of its effort to make sites generated through its platform more secure by default.

According to recent reports, “The moment real people use what you build, security is the product,” Igor Andriushchenko, Lovable’s head of security, tells WIRED. “That's why it's one of the areas we continue investing in the most and why we’ve built it directly into the platform experience.”.

According to recent reports, osika will see Lovable as successful next year if he can help a fresh wave of entrepreneurs start sustainable businesses. Why just vibe code an app when you can vibe code a living?

#23992. U.S. officially loses measles elimination status amid ongoing outbreaks

U.S. officially loses measles elimination status amid ongoing outbreaks

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • on Tuesday lost its official designation as a measles-free nation, more than 25 years after it eliminated the highly contagious virus.
  • The Pan American Health Organization unveiled the decision, which came after an independent panel of eight scientific experts convened last week to consider the country's epidemiological evidence.
  • In other words, measles is spreading regularly in the country again, with ongoing outbreaks sparking latest ones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S. on Tuesday lost its official designation as a measles-free nation, more than 25 years after it eliminated the highly contagious virus.

The Pan American Health Organization unveiled the decision, which came after an independent panel of eight scientific experts convened last week to consider the country's epidemiological evidence. The director of PAHO, the regional branch of the World Health Organization, made the final call that measles is endemic — or always present — in the U.S. following 12 months of continuous transmission.

In other words, measles is spreading regularly in the country again, with ongoing outbreaks sparking latest ones.

"The commission concluded that endemic measles transmission has now been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico and the United States, and recommended that their measles elimination status be withdrawn — a recommendation which I have accepted," Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO director, stated during a news briefing on Tuesday.

In a recent development, it's a devastating step backward for American public health, as declining childhood vaccination rates and vaccine hesitancy fuel outbreaks across the country that have sickened thousands of people and led to a tragic string of preventable deaths. Among the deaths where vaccination status was reported, all were unvaccinated.

Industry observers note that more than 5,400 measles cases had been reported nationwide in 2026 as of mid-November, marking the country's worst outbreak in more than three decades. States have confirmed 10 deaths associated with the disease so far in 2026: seven in Pennsylvania, one in New York and two in Wisconsin.

It has been revealed that the commission found that out of 52 U.S. states and territories it tracked, 48 experienced measles outbreaks during the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, PAHO Assistant Director Dr. Rhonda Sealey-Thomas said during the briefing. But Barbosa said the countries are already taking action to control outbreaks, such as strengthening vaccination, surveillance for timely case detection and outbreak response efforts.

It has been revealed that the U.S. in particular has ramped up vaccination efforts to close immunity gaps, particularly in areas with low immunization coverage experiencing outbreaks, said Dr. Daniel Salas, executive manager of PAHO's Special Program for Comprehensive Immunization. He said PAHO expects the U.S. to present its corrective action proposal in the coming weeks, outlining strategies to regain its designation.

In a Tuesday release, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said it will continue to ensure all communities have the resources to prevent and respond to outbreaks and is committed to working with states and other local partners to restore the U.S.'s measles elimination status.

CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said in the release that the measles elimination designation "is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does." She said the agency has invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach communities where transmission is occurring.

Last week, Schwartz told Reuters that the agency is going to be "doing the same exact thing that we've been doing today" if the U.S. loses its measles-free status.

The decision also poses a fresh test for the Trump administration and its Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has taken steps to change recommendations for the childhood measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine and has a long history of questioning its safety without evidence.

But Kennedy, in a Tuesday X post, mentioned he continues to recommend MMR vaccination as "the most effective way to prevent measles.".

Industry observers note that "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," Kennedy stated. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment.".

In a recent development, CNBC previously reported on how the return of measles in the U.S. exposes weaknesses in the nation's public health system that raise concerns about the return of other eliminated diseases. The resurgence of measles exposes eroding trust in health institutions and growing challenges in persuading people to protect themselves, their children and their communities.

Public health experts previously told CNBC that the return of measles ultimately boils down to fewer children getting vaccinated.

According to recent reports, the MMR vaccine is about 97% effective against measles after two doses, while a single dose is 93% effective, according to the CDC. Yet data aggregated by the CDC demonstrates that vaccination coverage for that shot among U.S. kindergarteners fell to 92.4% in the 2025-2026 school year, which is below the 95% threshold public health officials generally recommend to prevent sustained transmission.

The American Medical Association urged the public to get vaccinated after PAHO's announcement.

"We must treat the current measles outbreaks as an urgent call to rebuild trust in science-based recommendations and restore strong, fully-funded public health infrastructure to protect families and communities and prevent the return of diseases once eliminated," AMA President Dr. Willie Underwood noted in a statement.

In a separate statement, the pharmaceutical industry's largest lobbying group called on policymakers to provide "clear, accurate information about the seriousness of measles infection and the effectiveness of vaccines against it, restore and sustain high vaccination coverage in every community, strengthen vaccination efforts, and invest in disease surveillance and rapid outbreak response.".

Sources indicate that "We have the tools to eliminate measles again and what we need now is the commitment to use them," stated Dr. Michael Ybarra, chief medical officer of the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America.

Measles isn't just a public health threat — it's also a huge financial burden on the healthcare system, CNBC reported.

Industry observers note that based on this year's case count, a fresh tool developed by researchers at Johns Hopkins University estimates an economic cost of nearly $83 million for the outbreaks. That total includes $56 million in public health response costs, almost $25 million in lost productivity and more than $1.8 million in direct medical expenses.

The U.S. now joins Canada, Spain and the U.K., which all recently lost their measles-free status after a review by experts at the World Health Organization. While the U.S. dropped out of the WHO, it remains a member of PAHO, its Americas branch.

Emergency services were called to Cosy Toes nursery in Middleton, near Manchester on the afternoon of 2 November after “reports of a concern for a child”.

Industry observers note that greater Manchester police noted at the time that a child had been taken to hospital after a “medical emergency” and was in a critical condition. An investigation had been opened, GMP said, adding that “no arrests have made in that time”. The force said the investigation was in line with usual procedure, “as the circumstances leading up to the boy’s death occurred in a care setting”.

Det Ch Insp Claire Brennan said: “This is an incredibly tragic development in a deeply upsetting incident and our thoughts remain with the boy’s family.

It has been revealed that “We are in the very early stages of our involvement and are carefully considering events and the evidence available to us. For now, we ask that the family’s privacy is respected as they begin to navigate the unimaginable loss of their little boy.”.

Recent findings suggest that cosy Toes runs four nurseries in Middleton, providing childcare for children up to five years old. GMP has asked anyone with information that could help the investigation to make a report online, or call 0161 856 3635.

Details can also be given anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or by filling out a form on their website.

Cosy Toes has been approached for comment.

FAA pauses installation of fresh routers after ground stop

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Aviation Administration noted Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.
  • Industry observers note that tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy remarked Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration noted Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Industry observers note that tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy remarked Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news about the pause.

The FAA and Department of Transportation have said L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation this week asked the FAA and the Department of Transportation for clarity on what went wrong.

"Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," the senators wrote in a statement. "Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety.".

The agencies have said they are working to figure out the root cause of the issue and have reiterated that there is no indication of a cyberattack or outside threat.

The senators also asked for a briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper Networks, which is making the newly introduced devices, by Monday. They asked the companies to lay out why the operational systems lacked sufficient redundancy and answer other questions about what led to the outage.

CNBC has reached out to L3Harris and Juniper Networks for comment.

Duffy on Friday called for Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system, more than he has previously asked for. Democratic lawmakers pushed back on the request, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Senate Commerce Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, noted Tuesday that he thinks there will be support for air traffic control modernization, but that the allocation should be specifically for safety upgrades.

"I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded," he said. "Some of that is not safety related, but we just discussed there, and what I expressed is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.".

Sources indicate that duffy dismissed the idea that the router matter had to do with the introduction of artificial intelligence tools and said it was "completely unfounded" because the AI system is not in communication with the defective router. He added that the FBI is helping to investigate the root cause of the issue.

Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have for years angered airline executives, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

— CNBC's Phil LeBeau, Leslie Josephs and Justin Papp contributed to this report.

But that party—which was reportedly paid for by a Russian oligarch—has since turned into a legal and political headache.

Industry observers note that representative Robert Garcia, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee, also issued similar record-preservation requests to Eric Trump along with Donald Trump Jr., as cofounders of the wildly controversial crypto firm World Liberty Financial, and their brother-in-law Jared Kushner, who runs a Saudi-backed investment firm while serving as a presidential envoy to the Middle East. “As the President has said, he's willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans. After they won control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, Democrats made it plain that they were going to be beyond aggressive in ramping up their investigations. Now that they have the added resources and authority that come with being in the majority, Garcia and other Democrats want to dig into that growing fortune and who contributed to it.

In a recent development, senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has been looking into World Liberty and other Trump family crypto projects “for 18 months,” as a recent letter to the firm noted. Senator Elizabeth Warren has repeatedly called for investigations into World Liberty’s “national security risks,” including sales of its token to alleged North Korean hackers and Russian money launderers. Representative Ro Khanna wants to know more about the secret sale of 49 percent of World Liberty to funds controlled by Sheikh Tahnoun bin Zayed al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates’ intelligence chief, and whether that sale had anything to do with the Trump administration’s decision to allow the sale of advanced AI chips to Abu Dhabi.

Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789, went from a few hundred million under management to somewhere around $4 billion. The Trump Organization has real estate development deals underway from Bucharest to Bali.

The sudden influx of cash, Garcia notes in his letters, “raises serious concerns” that the deals are essentially “contributions to President Trump and his family in exchange for government action on behalf of the wealthy and well connected. Access to preferential treatment, federal secrets, regulatory law enforcement leniency, and the president and senior officials appears to trace back to suspicious activity associated with these schemes.”.

Industry observers note that the Trumps and their representatives have repeatedly insisted they’ve done nothing to merit this kind of scrutiny, other than have the wrong last name. “We've been dealing with the conflict-of-interest stuff for years,” Donald Trump Jr. told CNBC at a World Liberty Finance event at Mar-a-Lago in February. “Frankly, it's gotten old.”.

The Russian oligarch who paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding party later claimed the president’s son reimbursed him. “There is no evidence that any member of the Trump family ever sought to influence government policy or sought preferential treatment or government intervention to advance their personal or business interests,” Alan Garten, the Trump Organization’s chief legal officer, told this reporter prior to the election.

Sources indicate that the pushback from Trumpworld has grown more intense since the Democrats’ midterm sweep. Tech Report: Saudi Arabia: Rights groups raise alarm over rising number of executions

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that saudi Arabia continues to execute people at an alarming rate.
  • Recent findings suggest that the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention called for Qureiris' release in November 2024, after finding that his detention was arbitrary.
  • The two executions brought the number of people executed in Saudi Arabia in 2026 to 211, according to an AFP tally reported on Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that saudi Arabia continues to execute people at an alarming rate. On Saturday, Jawad Abdullah Qureiris and Fadel Hassan al-Safwani were executed in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. Both men were convicted of terrorist offenses, according to Saudi authorities. In 2011, al-Safwani was a prominent organizer of the peaceful protests that called for civil rights and the release of detainees. Qureiris, who was a minor at the time, participated in one of these protests in the city of Qatif.

Recent findings suggest that the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention called for Qureiris' release in November 2024, after finding that his detention was arbitrary. The opinion also covered four other men. Qureiris was the fourth of these five to be executed. The fifth, Yousef al-Manasif, remains at risk after Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court upheld his death sentence, according to human rights organizations.

The two executions brought the number of people executed in Saudi Arabia in 2026 to 211, according to an AFP tally reported on Monday. The news agency noted that the tally includes 126 people convicted of drug trafficking and 17 people executed on terrorism-related charges. Of the 211 people, 100 were Saudi nationals, while the rest were foreign nationals, AFP said.

Sources indicate that in July, Saudi authorities executed five Ethiopian migrants for nonviolent drug-related offenses, Human Rights Watch reported. In October, Saudi authorities executed two Bangladeshi nationals, according to rights organizations. Human Rights Watch separately reported the execution of another Saudi national, Hassan Zaki al-Faraj, on October 17, for alleged offenses committed when he was a minor.

"In 2025, a record high of at least 356 people were executed and executions have continued at a high rate in 2026," Ahmed Benchemsi, Human Rights Watch's MENA spokesperson, told DW. "Saudi Arabia has executed more than 2,000 people in the past decade," he confirmed.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, Saudi Arabia ranks third in executions after China and Iran. However, comprehensive global data for 2026 are not yet available, and many countries treat execution numbers as state secrets. However, the ranking is consistent with earlier findings from Amnesty International, which ranked Saudi Arabia as the world's third-most prolific executioner between 2022 and 2025, behind China and Iran.

According to the NGO Together against the death penalty, or ECPM, the two main methods of execution in Saudi Arabia are stoning or beheading. However, in many cases, including those of Qureiris and al-Safwani, death sentences are issued as discretionary rulings, called ta'zir. Ta'zir means that neither the crime nor the punishment is defined in Islamic law, contrary to fixed punishments under the Saudi interpretation of Islamic law, or Sharia. As a result, little to no information about the execution or the fate of the bodies is provided.

Recent findings suggest that following the US-Israeli attacks on Iran in February, Saudi Arabia has been targeted by Iran and the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen. In turn, Saudi Arabia's de facto leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, is faced with a profound dilemma as the attacks have killed and injured scores of people and threaten Riyadh's efforts to diversify its economy under the Vision 2030 reform proposal. Several summits and international sports events had to be canceled or postponed in light of the ongoing danger.

It has been revealed that "The Saudi government has shown itself to be unable to defend its population from repeated Houthi attacks on its airports, exposing the vulnerability of the country despite world-record spending levels on defense equipment," Sarah Leah Whitson, human rights lawyer and former executive director of the US-based human rights watchdog DAWN, told DW. "Amid the war in Iran, the Saudi government has resumed its relentless pace of executions and corporal punishment sentences," she remarked.

This week, watchdogs reported on a Kenyan woman in Saudi Arabia who was sentenced to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage.

"The recent executions and the sentencing of a migrant domestic worker to 100 lashes for having a child out of wedlock are clear indications that the Saudi government continues to rely on brute repression to rule the country," Whitson told DW.

Maryam Aldossari, acting director of the London-based human rights organization ALQST, echoes this view. "Saudi Arabian authorities have undoubtedly used the war in Iran and wider regional tensions to intensify their crackdown, most notably through their increased use of the death penalty and as a tool of political repression against the country's Shia minority," she told DW.

Industry observers note that saudi Arabia is predominantly Sunni. The country's oil-rich Eastern Province — from which the recently executed men Jawad Abdullah Qureiris and Fadel Hassan al-Safwani hailed — is home to most of Saudi Arabia's Shia minority. Iran, on the other hand, is predominantly Shia. Saudi authorities have long viewed some forms of Shia political activism with suspicion, partly because of concerns over Iranian influence and alleged links between domestic dissent and Tehran, accusations that rights groups say have been used to justify repression of the minority.

Industry observers note that however, Neil Quilliam, associate fellow in the Middle East and North Africa Programme at the London-based think tank Chatham House, remains cautious about drawing a direct causal connection between the conflict involving Iran and developments in Saudi Arabia's human rights environment. "The kingdom has introduced social reforms over the past decade, including measures that have expanded opportunities for women, while retaining controls over political dissent and activism," he told DW.

According to recent reports, "What periods of regional tension can do is heighten official concern about national security," he mentioned, adding that this reduces tolerance for any public criticism or perceived threats to social cohesion. "Whether that amounts to a change in the human rights situation is harder to demonstrate, but there is certainly a sense among some observers that space for dissent has become even more constrained, not only in Saudi Arabia, but in other Gulf states too," he said.

DW reached out to Saudi Arabia's Human Rights Commission on Monday, November, 16, 2026 but has not received an answer at the time of publication.

Building AI that can work across the enterprise

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments.
  • For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects.
  • In a recent development, that foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model.

For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he states, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. For some everyday applications, “80% might be good enough,” he says, but in areas such as supply chains or financial close, that level of accuracy is “a very terrible result.”.

In a recent development, that foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing. Satinder Pal Singh, associate VP North America for SAP BAIP and SAP AI Strategy at Infosys, frames AI agents as “digital coworkers” and recommends evaluating potential use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. Companies should identify where an agent can move meaningful business metrics, determine whether their data and talent can support the use case, and then establish whether successful applications can be replicated. “A pilot that can't scale is just an experiment,” he says.

Scaling also brings governance into sharper focus. Clear policies, access controls, monitoring, and oversight are necessary to ensure agents remain trustworthy and aligned with business requirements. “The absence of governance doesn't speed up AI adoption,” Singh indicates. “It creates a risk backlog” that can ultimately force a more disruptive stop and audit.

Those considerations will become more important as AI agents take on more responsibilities as digital coworkers. Both executives see a future in which agentic systems coordinate work across applications, while customer-specific knowledge graphs and governed data become critical enterprise assets. For Singh, the longer-term opportunity is a shift from AI as a productivity tool to “AI as a decision-making partner,” helping leaders understand what is happening, anticipate what comes next, and determine how to respond.

Booking Holdings creates new enterprise division as AI reshapes travel planning

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Booking Holdings is bringing together two of its business-to-business travel operations in a fresh division it hopes will be transformational, betting that a larger, coordinated partner platform can generate growth as artificial intelligence changes how travelers discover and book trips.
  • Sources indicate that the new enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January.
  • "We realize that if we focus our efforts both on the product side, but also on the go-to-market side, then we can potentially grow faster and serve better partners," Morgenshtern told CNBC in an exclusive interview.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Booking Holdings is bringing together two of its business-to-business travel operations in a fresh division it hopes will be transformational, betting that a larger, coordinated partner platform can generate growth as artificial intelligence changes how travelers discover and book trips.

Sources indicate that the new enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January. Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern will lead the unit, which aims to help businesses such as banks, airlines and online travel companies sell trips or build branded experiences for their customers.

"We realize that if we focus our efforts both on the product side, but also on the go-to-market side, then we can potentially grow faster and serve better partners," Morgenshtern told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

He said existing partners will find new and better products, which will also help grow the partner base.

According to recent reports, the move gives Booking a single organization to coordinate technology, travel supply and commercial expertise across business relationships. The company says partners will be able to use its global supply and technology through white-label platforms, integrated applications, branded solutions and hotel-chain rate distribution.

The portfolio includes more than 4.7 million properties, 33 million accommodation listings, more than 500 airlines and more than 200 car rental providers, according to the company.

Competitor Expedia Group has seen notable growth by prioritizing its enterprise efforts, including a strategy launched in 2022 to make its technology platform available to business partners looking to add travel to their own offerings.

From 2018 to 2023, Expedia’s business-to-business revenue grew at a 16% compound annual rate, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, for the division grew at a 28% rate, the organization said in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025, Expedia’s B2B revenue rose 18% to $4.8 billion, and its segment adjusted EBITDA increased 22% to $1.26 billion. Those figures represented about a third of Expedia’s total revenue and more than a third of its adjusted EBITDA for the full year.

Morgenshtern declined to say how much the newly introduced division is expected to contribute to Booking Holdings' overall revenue and profit, but he remarked the opportunity for growth is immense, estimating the total addressable market at $2 trillion.

Online travel agencies have been pressured this year as investors scrutinize how AI will change the way customers search for and then book their travel.

Companies that offer lodging, experiences and other travel and leisure are grappling with how to stay visible if AI tools become the upcoming starting point for planning and reservations.

Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro said on the firm’s earnings call Tuesday that guests already use AI to discover and strategy Disney trips, and that some are using the tools to book.

“Ultimately, we want Disney to show up in those tools,” he stated, adding that Disney is exploring ways to let guests make reservations directly from them.

Booking anticipates offering partners AI capabilities that draw on the firm's existing travel know-how while minimizing token costs, it noted.

It has been revealed that "I see a lot of AI demos," Morgenshtern remarked, drawing a distinction between a product that caters to a few customers and one that's scalable and works even when overloaded by travel emergencies. He said he's "super optimistic" about the bespoke product — a vertical agent — that Booking will offer to its partners.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Page-turn remotes are one of the hottest accessories for e-readers.
  • E-reader aficionados on BookTok create the coziest winter reading setups with e-reader stands and remotes so they don't have to hold their Kindle for reading marathons.
  • Recent findings suggest that but clearly it hasn't taken long for e-reader makers to finally meet the moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Page-turn remotes are one of the hottest accessories for e-readers. In the past year, not one or two, but three e-reader brands have debuted remotes to pair with e-readers.

E-reader aficionados on BookTok create the coziest winter reading setups with e-reader stands and remotes so they don't have to hold their Kindle for reading marathons. When these reading setups first became popular, no e-reader brand had rolled out a native remote, so customers were turning to Amazon and TikTok Shop for their gear from third-party manufacturers.

Recent findings suggest that but clearly it hasn't taken long for e-reader makers to finally meet the moment. Kobo was first, with Boox following soon after. Amazon, surprisingly, was the last to join in on the fun. I have had the pleasure of trying all of these remotes with their corresponding e-readers and learned that they're not all created equal. Each brand has a different approach to design and functionality, and some are far more functional than others.

According to recent reports, so I tested three Bluetooth page-turn remotes for e-readers and ranked my favorites. But keep in mind that these remotes are designed to work exclusively with their brand's e-readers, so which one you buy depends on which e-reader you have.

Recent findings suggest that the Boox Tappy is a funny little gadget that looks more like a mini typewriter than it does a remote. It's compatible with Boox e-readers (we like the Boox Go 6) and the keys on the remote are customizable. The most common use is letting the pages turn forward and back, but you can also set them to adjust the volume and scroll web pages.

Industry observers note that while I appreciate the versatility of the remote, it's not quite functional. I found it finicky when not using it with books in the native Boox library. The remote isn't compatible with every app on Boox devices either, so I could use it when reading my Kindle books but not on the Libby app.

In a recent development, however, to turn the page on Kindle, it does require some workarounds, too. I had to change the settings in the Kindle app so that the volume buttons turned the page.

Industry observers note that once you have the Tappy fully set up, it works pretty seamlessly; however, it is the least ergonomic remote, and I found my hand cramping up when using it for more than 30 minutes. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Compatible with: Note Air5 C, Palma 2 Pro, and other Boox devices with Firmware V4.2 or later that support Bluetooth functionality.

Kobo was the first to make a remote made for its own e-readers. The Kobo Remote has two buttons: a larger one to turn the page forward and a second smaller button to turn the page back. It has a classic, remote look with a slightly curved design. It also has a wrist lanyard so it can stay on you in case you fall asleep while reading — safe to say that's come in handy for me quite a few times.

In a recent development, that curve adds some necessary ergonomics to the remote, as it fits along the natural curve of your hand rather than straining your hand into one position. It connects via Bluetooth and stays ready to use at nearly any time. Just press any button once to wake the remote, and it should connect immediately.

The Kobo Remote works seamlessly and is extremely responsive. Plus, with the different-sized buttons, you can easily feel for the controls without looking. If you're a Kobo e-reader user, the Kobo Remote is an essential accessory, although it's not my favorite e-reader remote.

Compatible with: Any Kobo e-reader with Bluetooth, which includes the Kobo Clara 2E, Kobo Clara BW, Kobo Clara Colour, Kobo Libra 2, Kobo Libra Colour, Kobo Sage, Kobo Elipsa, and Kobo Elipsa 2E.

Amazon took its time releasing the Kindle Click, an e-reader remote compatible with its 2024 or newer e-readers. It takes a similar design approach to the Kobo Remote with a long, rectangular form. The Kindle Click doesn't have the same ergonomic curvature as the Kobo Remote, but it's still comfortable and also has a wrist lanyard.

Recent findings suggest that it has two buttons with a different texture than the rest of the remote, so even though they're the same size, you can feel them easily. The buttons are customizable, so you can adjust which turns the page forward and which navigates backward. But my favorite part of the remote is the two small side buttons that control the brightness of your Kindle.

Being able to adjust the brightness on a Kindle is a huge boon since when I'm reading in bed — usually in the dark — the two things I need to do are turn the page and adjust the screen brightness. Being able to do so on one remote is extremely convenient and means my hands can stay warm under the blankets.

Compatible with: Kindle e-readers released in 2024 or later.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Best Smart Bed of 2026: Bryte and Tempur-Pedic

📅 09 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1333 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that while they may not be able to levitate or act like a Jetsons-style robot personal assistant (yet), smart beds these days come pretty close to accomplishing both.
  • The best smart bed is, by far, the Bryte Balance Pro Smart Mattress, and if you’re looking for the most luxurious, it’s the Tempur-Pedic Tempur-ActiveBreeze.
  • For more old-school mattresses, check out our guides to the Best Mattresses, the Best Organic Mattresses, and the Best Mattresses for Back Pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while they may not be able to levitate or act like a Jetsons-style robot personal assistant (yet), smart beds these days come pretty close to accomplishing both. Like adjustable mattresses, smart beds offer modifiable firmness and the ability to raise and lower the head and foot. These days, though, smart beds offer so much more, integrating features like dual-climate control, sleep tracking, and massage therapies.

The best smart bed is, by far, the Bryte Balance Pro Smart Mattress, and if you’re looking for the most luxurious, it’s the Tempur-Pedic Tempur-ActiveBreeze. Let me break it down for you below.

For more old-school mattresses, check out our guides to the Best Mattresses, the Best Organic Mattresses, and the Best Mattresses for Back Pain.

In a recent development, updated November 2026: I’ve updated product information and the FAQ section. Discontinued products were removed, and I updated specs, prices, and links.

I’m at the moment testing the Eight Sleep Pod 6.

In a recent development, most smart beds on the market use air chambers on each side of the mattress to achieve adjustable firmness. This is fine, but you can definitely feel them beneath you. But that's not the case with Bryte's Balance Pro, which is why it's so great.

Instead of air chambers, this smart bed is designed with coils (Bryte Balancers) and memory foam layers. These coils can be adjusted to specific zones, and if you want extra lumbar support or contouring, you can customize each section through the companion app. There are also 100 firmness levels, which makes it suitable for a variety of sleepers, from belly sleepers to larger-bodied individuals who may find air-chambered beds too soft.

Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes’ favorite feature is the massage function, which gently presses the coils against you. The smart bed is controlled exclusively via app, where you can also view your sleep insights. Along with metrics like sleep stages, duration, and heart rate, it also tracks the number of bed rebalances, which is how many times the Bryte Balancers are auto-adjusted throughout the night. There’s also an AI Sleep Concierge that is best for getting tips on how to sleep better.

Bryte Balance Pro ranges from $5,999 for a twin mattress to $6,899 for a California king.

Hot sleepers and overheaters will love Tempur-Pedic's Tempur-ActiveBreeze. There are fans built into the adjustable base that disperse cool or warm air, with three airflow speeds (slow, medium, and fast). The airflow is streamlined from the base through two ports in the bed, and the perforated memory foam layers and coils help promote circulation. According to the manufacturer, the dual climate control offers a 30-degree temperature range, which is the largest we’ve come across in testing. Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes could feel the air lightly skittering along the surface. On the bright side, even when she piled on her heaviest bedding, she didn’t run hot once.

According to recent reports, the Tempur-ActiveBreeze also offers sleep tracking, AI coaching, and a suite of relaxation programs that combine meditative soundscapes and massage therapy to lull you to sleep. Probably most notably, there’s an automatic snore response, which raises your head if it detects a breathing disturbance. The companion app breaks down your sleep data into digestible nightly, monthly, and annual reports.

The Tempur-ActiveBreeze (base included via Tempur-Pedic) ranges from $10,398 for a queen to $19,396 for a split California king.

Personal Comfort (The Rejuvenate).

Personal Comfort (Power-Flex 4 base).

Personal Comfort’s Rejuvenate is a solid adjustable mattress for side sleepers. It doesn’t offer any additional features or sleep-tracking capabilities, so it doesn’t truly qualify as a smart bed in my book.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, the Rejuvenate is a side-sleeper-friendly option because of its deep memory foam layers that contour to the body. If you want to sink in while still relying on the 45 firmness levels to ensure you're getting the support you need, this is it. Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes found a medium-firm 30 to be ideal for a healthy spine alignment when side sleeping.

What About Personal Comfort’s Adjustable Base?

An adjustable base is available as an add-on and helpful if you opt for one of Personal Comfort’s specialty bed sizes, such as the Queen Flex-Head or King Flex-Head. It’s the only way to move the head and foot of the Rejuvenate, as well as implement adjustable lumbar support, pillow tilt, and massage features.

Sources indicate that julia tested the Power Flex 4. It provides a firmer feel right around the midsection, and its lumbar adjustment setting really amps up back support. She did find the massage features to be uncomfortable, though, describing them as “increasingly aggressive vibrations, akin to tectonic plates.”.

FYI, Personal Comfort often runs a bundle promotion.

Should I Use a Sleep Tracker With a Smart Bed?

Some smart beds offer contactless sleep tracking, which eliminates the need for an additional wearable. That said, they do carry some limitations. They’re generally not as accurate as contact-based trackers and can overestimate sleep stages and miscalculate duration. They often can’t track the same breadth of physiological measurements as smartwatches and smart rings do. And they can misattribute data from a partner or pet sharing the bed. But they’re convenient, especially if you dislike wearing trackers to bed.

Personally, I still sleep with my Apple Watch Series 12 and/or Oura Ring 5 to bed to compare. But, if I forget to wear either, my smart bed is auto-tracking my slumber in the background.

Do I Need an Adjustable Base to Go With My Smart Bed?

You are very likely going to want an adjustable base to go with your smart bed in order to enjoy everything your smart bed has to offer. This is especially true if you are purchasing one with the expectation of being able to move the top and bottom of the bed into different angles, like “TV watching” and “zero gravity” settings.

What’s the Difference Between an Adjustable Bed and a Smart Bed?

Generally speaking, adjustable beds and smart beds are similar in that they both can raise or lower different sections of your mattress, with a remote control or companion app. Smart beds take it up a notch by incorporating additional features, such as sleep tracking, temperature control, and automated adjustments.

Can a Smart Bed Work for All Sleeping Positions?

Sources indicate that smart beds often come in adjustable firmness levels, and therefore can work for all sleeping positions. However, just like with any other mattress, the fabric technology is a huge deciding factor when it comes to comfort.

Industry observers note that for example, the Bryte Balance Pro is a much better choice for stomach sleepers or if you have a heavier body type. Coil support simply does not compare to even the firmest of inflated air chambers, which are usually what make smart beds' firmness levels “adjustable.” On the other hand, the Rejuvenate has a softer feel right off the bat because of its memory foam layers, making it ideal for side sleepers who need pressure relief.

Do I Need Wi-Fi Connectivity for My Smart Bed to Work?

Yes—if the power goes out, your smart bed will likely go offline. Smart beds are factored into smart home technology, meaning they rely on Wi-Fi for full functionality, especially to track sleep data and maintain the firmness level you've chosen.

What Does WIRED Do With the Mattresses After Testing Them?

According to recent reports, these smart beds were provided for free as media samples, and we either return them to the company or donate without personal benefit when testing is done. Most of these beds went to nurses, students, families in need, or those with medical conditions that were affecting their sleep.
