What President Trump appeared to lack in enthusiasm, his hosts in the Philippines made up for in hospitality by catering to his preferences during a brief state visit.

The president stopped in Manila on his way to a historic meeting with the autocratic leaders of Russia and China in Shenzhen, just as the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, was wrapping up.

He did not even go to the summit venue; Southeast Asian leaders met him at the hotel where he was staying.

Sources indicate that when President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines rushed to leave a news conference after wrapping up the ASEAN summit, he told reporters: “I cannot keep the president of the United States waiting. Sorry.”.

Industry observers note that for Mr. Marcos and much of the region, flattering Mr. Trump is part of a strategy of balancing the United States and China.

It has been revealed that although Mr. Marcos has called for a reset of relations with China, tensions remain high with Beijing over territorial claims in the South China Sea.

“Whether they like it or not, the Philippines is a traditional U.S. ally,” said Georgi Engelbrecht, a Philippines analyst at the International Crisis Group, a think tank. “China will never trust it strategically.”.

The Philippines and the United States are bound by a 75-year-old mutual defense treaty.

In remarks before their bilateral meeting on Wednesday, Mr. Marcos seemed to make an effort to use language that would please his guest, referring to A.I. as “super intelligence,” a term Mr. Trump has made mandatory for his government.

Tapping into Mr. Trump’s predilection for fast food, Mr. Marcos remarked he had sent Mr. Trump fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee. “It’s providing extra energy for all the work that is in front of you,” Mr. Marcos said to the president at their meeting the next day.

Recent findings suggest that during his roughly three-minute speech, Mr. Marcos brought up Mr. Trump’s “brief stop” in Manila at least six times.

Industry observers note that for his part, Mr. Trump was also complimentary, telling Mr. Marcos that he was well acquainted with his parents, the dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos and his wife, Imelda Marcos, who came to be known for her shoe collection and unexplained wealth.

“You have very good genetics, I can tell you that,” Mr. Trump told Mr. Marcos at a dinner with Southeast Asian leaders on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, “Personal chemistry and rapport between leaders is important,” remarked Lucio Pitlo III, the president of ThinkSea Consulting, a Philippine think tank. “But leveraging them to tangibly advance national interests is the more crucial metric.”.

Sources indicate that he said Mr. Marcos’s efforts to have good relations with Mr. Trump had paid off in the past, for example, in a proposed U.S. tariff rate that was half as much as in other parts of the region.

Filipinos have traditionally viewed the United States, its former colonial ruler, more favorably than they view China. But punishing tariffs and higher fuel prices as a result of the war in Iran have been difficult for the country to absorb.

According to recent reports, after his meeting with Mr. Marcos, Mr. Trump confirmed that the two sides had signed “a very big ⁠trade deal.” Mr. Marcos’s office described it a an “understanding on key areas of economic cooperation.”.

Sources indicate that personal diplomacy was on display again later in the day. Mr. Trump briefly spoke with Imelda Marcos, 97, who is now rarely seen in public. As he left, she blew him a kiss from her wheelchair.

Industry observers note that xi Jinping told President Trump that he took the unusual move for a Chinese leader of greeting him at the airport because the American president had done the same for him when he visited the United States in September. “China is a nation of etiquette with a tradition of reciprocity,” Xi mentioned, according to Chinese state media.

President Trump is arriving at the summit as his envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, face headwinds in trying to negotiate a peace deal with Russia to end the war in Ukraine. Kushner and Witkoff went to Moscow last week to seek Putin’s approval to add the Europeans to talks, but Kremlin officials publicly rebuffed the request.

Putin’s arrival was accompanied by the same orchestra playing the trepak, or Russian dance melody, from Pyotr Tchaikovsky’s “The Nutcracker.”.

Sources indicate that xi Jinping, the Chinese leader, welcomed guests in Shenzhen, where President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia arrived and shook hands with President Trump.

President Trump walked into the event on a red carpet as a Chinese orchestra played a rendition of “America the Beautiful.”.

Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada has advanced his goal of reducing Canada’s economic reliance on the United States during a weeklong swing through Asia, emerging with trade deals with China and the Philippines.

But he was also presented with an unexpected opportunity to improve relations with Washington. On Wednesday, Mr. Carney declared that he would meet with President Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, leaving open the prospect of Canada starting to mend the rift with its neighbor.

“We have long said, and believed and still believe, that there is a mutually beneficial agreement between Canada and the United States in the context of the newly introduced U.S. trade policy,” Mr. Carney told reporters. “We’ll have discussions on that. And, we will do what’s necessary in order to achieve that deal, but only if that deal that is in the interest of Canadians.”.

It has been revealed that hours later, Mr. Carney’s office issued a brief statement confirming that the two leaders met and “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement.” It offered no details.

Before Wednesday, Mr. Carney’s aides said there was no expectation of a meeting with Mr. Trump in China. At the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in South Korea last year, the two men only spoke informally during a dinner.

According to recent reports, how much progress, if any, will result from the meeting is unclear. Before the encounter, Mr. Carney described dealing with the Trump administration on trade as a “two steps forward, one step back type thing.”.

Since his return to office, Mr. Trump has imposed a variety of tariffs on a wide range of Canadian products. While those tariffs have been effectively suspended for many goods that qualify as being made in North America, the suspension has not applied to the key auto, steel and aluminum industries. Their products face tariffs of up to 50 percent.

Negotiations between the two countries collapsed in August with each side pointing fingers at the other for the failure.

At the beginning of this month, Mr. Carney remarked that talks would restart after Mr. Trump said the United States would back off on some secondary problems that were irritants for Canada, including requirements relating to the promotion of Canadian and French language content on digital streaming services.

There has been little apparent activity since then but Mr. Carney mentioned on Wednesday that “we have been making progress.”.

Recent findings suggest that much more obvious has been the progress Mr. Carney has made with China. Before he took office, diplomatic incidents — including what was widely seen in Canada as the hostage-taking of two Canadians by China in 2018 — and Canada’s decision to follow the United States with 100 percent tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles had brought relations between the two countries to a near standstill.

But this week, at his second formal meeting with President Xi Jinping of China this year, Mr. Carney walked away with a second reduction in Chinese tariffs aimed at a variety of farm and fish products. The deal effectively marked the end of the trade war sparked by the auto tariff, Mr. Carney said, opening the door to an expanded trade relationship between the countries.

Recent findings suggest that mr. Carney also repeated this week that if Canada were unable to persuade Mr. Trump to end tariffs on its auto exports, it would look to China, Japan and Europe to keep Canada’s auto industry afloat.

Sources indicate that that suggestion drew criticism from Peter Navarro, a senior adviser to Mr. Trump.

“Are u really threatening to play China off the U.S.?” Mr. Navarro said in a social media post. “This is offensive in the extreme. You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive — as it is already doing.” Pete Hoekstra, Washington’s ambassador to Canada who has frequently offended Canadians, shared the post.

On Wednesday, however, Mr. Carney dismissed suggestions that Canada’s renewed relationship with China was poisoning its economically vital relationship with the United States.

In a recent development, “In my conversations with the president, he’s tried to understand where we are with China, where we’re going with China,” Mr. Carney mentioned. “I shouldn’t speak for him, but in his hierarchy of issues, it’s not the top issue at all.”.

Industry observers note that but selling the benefits of China back home may not be so easy. A recent poll found that only 14 percent of Canadians want closer trade ties with China. By contrast, 58 percent back Mr. Carney’s push for a closer relationship with the European Union.

After noting that Canadian fishermen and farmers strongly favor more trade with China, Mr. Carney downplayed the extent of the trade relationship.

“Relative to many other countries, our trade with China is quite modest and the breadth of it is quite modest.”.

Yuri Ushakov, a top aide to President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, told Russian state news media that Putin may speak with President Trump at a dinner for leaders in Shenzhen this evening before their formal meeting on Thursday.

When President Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi Jinping was waiting for him at the bottom of the steps descending from Air Force One.

Recent findings suggest that it was the first time that Mr. Xi had personally received a foreign dignitary at the airport in more than a decade as China’s leader. Visiting leaders are usually welcomed by senior Chinese officials and greeted by Mr. Xi at the Great Hall of the People in central Beijing.

Mr. Xi’s appearance, while unusual, was likely about reciprocating Mr. Trump’s hospitality. When Mr. Xi traveled to Washington for a state visit in September, Mr. Trump greeted the Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews. That was the first time the U.S. president had personally greeted a foreign visitor upon their arrival.

In a recent development, after Air Force One landed in Shenzhen for the last stop on his whirlwind trip to Asia, Mr. Xi rolled up to the tarmac in a black luxury sedan made by the Chinese carmaker Hongqi, or Red Flag. He walked toward the president’s plane along a red carpet flanked by young men and women cheering and waving American and Chinese flags. After Mr. Trump walked down the stairs from his plane toward Mr. Xi, the two shook hands. Mr. Trump patted Mr. Xi on the back before the two embraced.

Wu Xinbo, the dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai, said the leaders’ personal receptions reflected a shift in the U.S.-China relationship to focus on “respect, fairness, and reciprocity.”.

Recent findings suggest that mr. Wu noted that Mr. Xi’s presence was also likely a message of support for the American president, to show that China will “still treat him seriously and would like to continue to work with him,” after the Republican Party suffered a bruising defeat in the recent midterm elections.

The high-level reception accorded to Mr. Trump was a step up from the welcome given to President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, who arrived earlier on Wednesday. Mr. Putin was greeted by Cai Qi, a longtime deputy of Mr. Xi and one of the most influential officials in the Chinese leader’s inner circle. Mr. Cai is a member of the powerful Politburo Standing Committee, the Chinese Communist Party’s top echelon.

When Mr. Trump visited China in May, he was greeted by China’s vice president, Han Zheng, a ceremonial figurehead who often attends formal diplomatic events. When he visited in 2017, the president was greeted by Yang Jiechi, China’s then-top diplomat and a member of the Politburo, the party’s second-most powerful body.

Industry observers note that in 2009, when Mr. Xi was vice president and already seen as the likely successor to China’s leader at the time, Hu Jintao, Mr. Xi waited at the airport to greet President Barack Obama on his arrival in Beijing.

President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

In a recent development, mr. Putin arrived early Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, for a regional economic meeting and a trilateral summit with President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China. Satellite images demonstrated that two Russian Tu-95MS strategic nuclear bombers had landed on Tuesday at Da Nang Airport in nearby Vietnam alongside two long-range transport aircraft.

It was the first time that Russian strategic nuclear bombers had deployed to Vietnam since the Soviet era, a pointed demonstration of Russia’s nuclear might and global reach ahead of the high-level talks.

The surprise arrival of the Russian aircraft in the region caused a scramble among American allies in Asia.

Japan dispatched jets after Russian planes were detected in Japanese airspace near Okinoshima, an island in the south of Japan, and Tokyo registered its discontent with the Russian authorities. South Korea also deployed fighter jets; the authorities there noted the Russian planes entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone, where Seoul closely monitors foreign aircraft, but not its sovereign airspace.

Recent findings suggest that russia lags both China and the United States significantly in economic output, technological innovation, population size and trade flows, making Mr. Putin’s participation in the trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday to some degree conspicuous.

In a recent development, but the one critical area where Russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Russia boasts the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal, which Mr. Putin has brandished as a reason the world must continue to accord Moscow a certain level of deference and respect. Russia has also developed a range of latest nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

It has been revealed that the Tu-95MS is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

Taiwan on Tuesday said it detected two sorties of Russian military aircraft flying in airspace east of the island. Gen. Huang Chih-wei, the Vice Chief of the Taiwanese military’s General Staff, said that “the actions of the Russian aircraft undermine regional peace and stability and are detrimental to maintaining the status quo of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.”.

The Russian and Vietnamese authorities did not make any public statements about the arrival of the bombers. Mr. Putin met with Vietnam’s leader, To Lam, in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi are also attending.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

For Vietnam, the decision to welcome the Russian nuclear bombers shows China that Vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by Beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.

But it is a careful balancing act for the Vietnamese.

Recent findings suggest that vietnam allowed Russia to refuel its bombers from Cam Ranh Bay in 2014 as they patrolled the area around Guam, but the refueling was done midair and the bombers did not land on Vietnamese soil. At the time, the United States protested the use of Cam Ranh Bay, a former American and then Soviet base, for the refueling.

Reporting was contributed by Javier C. Hernández in Tokyo, Chris Buckley in Taipei, Taiwan, Choe Sang-Hun in Seoul and Tung Ngo in Hanoi, Vietnam.

In a recent development, when Imelda Marcos and Donald J. Trump partied in Upcoming York in the 1990s, she was the exiled former first lady of the Philippines, the wife of an ousted dictator, and he was a real estate mogul facing multiple bankruptcies.

They met again in Manila on Wednesday in vastly different roles. Mr. Trump, 80, is, of course, the president of the United States. And Ms. Marcos, 97, is the mother of the president of the Philippines, her family ensconced again in Malacañang Palace.

They had a brief conversation, according to a video posted on social media by a White House aide. It showed President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines walking Mr. Trump to where Ms. Marcos was waiting in a wheelchair.

In a recent development, “Mom,” Mr. Marcos, 69, mentioned as he ushered Mr. Trump toward her. He has said that Mr. Trump knows his mother “very well.”.

Recent findings suggest that ms. Marcos has rarely been seen in public after she was hospitalized with pneumonia in 2024.

“Welcome to the Philippines,” she told Mr. Trump. She handed him a gift and blew him a kiss as he walked away with her son.

“She’s always the most beautiful,” Mr. Trump mentioned.

Industry observers note that ms. Marcos wielded immense power when her husband was president and came to be known for her flamboyant lifestyle, shoe collection and unexplained wealth.

Mr. Trump, who was in the Philippines for a brief state visit, has made clear that he admires the Marcos family, part of his well-known affinity for autocratic leaders. On Tuesday night, he mentioned to Mr. Marcos: “I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great.” He went on, “I believe in genetics. They did a good job. You have very good genetics, I can tell you that.”.

In a recent development, earlier on Wednesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in Manila that Trump was willing to meet with Kim Jong Un, the leader of North Korea, to resolve issues. However, Rubio did not say whether a meeting between Trump and Kim was likely to happen.

According to recent reports, “The president has never viewed meeting and talking to someone as a concession,” Rubio remarked. “How are you going to solve problems with people you have disagreements with if you don’t speak to them?”.

Industry observers note that xi’s decision to personally greet Trump at the airport is unusual. He did not come himself when Trump visited Beijing in May. But Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Xi in September, a rare move for any American president and the first time Trump had done so for a foreign visitor.

Trump was greeted upon his arrival in Shenzhen by Xi, in an unusually high-level welcome ceremony. Foreign leaders are usually received by senior Chinese officials, not Xi himself.

President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines said on Wednesday that he had fried chicken delivered to President Trump during his overnight stay in Manila.

Sources indicate that it wasn’t just any fried chicken. It came from Jollibee, a chain that is considered a national treasure in the Philippines.

According to recent reports, “Since you’re strapped for time, I thought a taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late night snack for you and your delegation,” Mr. Marcos noted in his remarks before a meeting with Mr. Trump.

According to recent reports, it was not clear if Mr. Trump actually ate any.

Mr. Marcos’s gesture was not only a matter of national pride, but also appeared to be a nod to Mr. Trump’s well-documented fondness for fast food. Mr. Trump, a self-described germaphobe, has mentioned that he favors fast food from chains like McDonald’s because of their speed, consistency and hygiene.

In April, he received two McDonald’s bags delivered by DoorDash to the Oval Office, in an event the White House had staged to promote a Trump administration initiative that removed taxes on overtime and tips.

“I like cleanliness, and I think you’re better off going there than maybe someplace that you have no idea where the food’s coming from. It’s a certain standard,” Mr. Trump said in a 2016 interview with CNN. Later that year, he posted a photo of himself on social media enjoying a bucket of Kentucky Fried Chicken on his private plane.

Sources indicate that mr. Marcos told Mr. Trump on Wednesday that Jollibee had surpassed Kentucky Fried Chicken in popularity in the United States. The claim was dubious but Mr. Trump replied: “Oh, wow, fantastic.”.

While KFC still has many more stores than Jollibee in the United States, the Filipino chain has promoted its fried chicken as America’s best since at least 2022, citing food critics’ rankings and three consecutive wins in a USA Today readers’ poll.

On its home turf, Jollibee far outpaces American fast-food chains in store count and revenue. To compete with Jollibee in the Philippines, McDonald’s has altered its local menu to offer a sweeter hamburger sauce, fried chicken and rice, and Filipino-style sweet spaghetti.

Jollibee has expanded beyond the Philippines by acquiring food brands in countries such as the United States, China and South Korea, including the Colorado-based burger chain Smashburger and the Hong Kong dim sum chain Tim Ho Wan.

It has been revealed that mr. Marcos’s shout-out came as Jollibee is exploring a Hong Kong Stock Exchange listing for its international business, after initially saying it would list in the United States. The firm’s founder and chairman, Tony Tan Caktiong, said in September that the change reflected Asian investors’ familiarity with the brand.

Industry observers note that jollibee has not opened any stores in Washington, though there are several in Latest York, Mr. Trump’s home state, and Florida, where he spends a lot of time.

It has been revealed that xi mentioned in a meeting with Putin that relations between China and Russia have remained as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain,” according to Chinese state media. Xi called for the two sides to advance “world multipolarity” and the “democratization of international relations,” terms Xi uses to describe a world order in which the United States is less dominant.

Recent findings suggest that at a lunch with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines on Wednesday, Trump mentioned that the two countries had unexpectedly signed a new trade deal. Marcos’s office later said that the deal would cover energy and food security, without providing further details.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t know that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal for both,” Trump mentioned during the lunch. He later said on social media that the deal would benefit American farmers.

Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada told reporters that he would meet with Trump on Wednesday in Shenzhen to discuss the trade dispute between the two countries.

China warned on Tuesday that it could hit back after the Trump administration this week proposed a rule that would restrict China’s access to advanced chips through data centers outside its borders.

China’s ministry of commerce noted the rule went against the terms that China and the United States had agreed to in a fragile truce that expires in two months. “If the US persists, China will take countermeasures,” a ministry spokesman said.

China experts warned that the rule, the latest in a series of escalatory moves from both sides, would make it harder for Xi and Trump to come to any meaningful agreement to deescalate conflict between the world’s biggest economies.

Industry observers note that in a sign of Putin’s importance to Xi, the Russian leader was greeted at the airport in Shenzhen on Wednesday by Cai Qi, one of the seven members of the elite Politburo Standing Committee. That appears to make Cai the highest-ranking official to greet a foreign leader at APEC so far ahead of Trump’s arrival, according to a review of Chinese state media.

Cai is considered one of the most influential figures in Xi’s inner circle, having served as a deputy to the Chinese leader when he was a provincial official. He accompanied Xi to Washington in September.

Sources indicate that this is not the first time Cai has welcomed a foreign leader on the tarmac. Last year, he and Wang Yi, China’s top diplomat, greeted North Korea’s Kim Jong-un when he landed in Beijing.

Putin and Xi are expected to tour the campus that Moscow State University, Russia’s top university, set up in Shenzhen with the Beijing Institute of Technology. The leaders agreed to establish it a decade ago. The Shenzhen outpost looks like a mini version of the Moscow university, complete with a replica of its Stalin-era tower.

Putin and his team held talks with Xi followed by a smaller working breakfast. They have met dozens of times; this is at least their fourth in-person meeting this year. The talks lasted more than two hours, according to the Russian state news agency Tass.

World leaders coming to Shenzhen this week are arriving in an almost spotless, ultramodern metropolis, its streets bedecked with pastel banners but mostly emptied of the crowds typical of many Chinese cities.

Sources indicate that shenzhen lies slightly closer to the Equator than Havana, providing a balmy venue for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering. Under sunny skies with mild temperatures, a festive mood prevails in the city, which bears a strong resemblance to Miami — only much larger and with taller, newer high-rises.

In a recent development, schools in Shenzhen have closed this week, many residents have left town and local authorities have instructed companies to allow those employees who are still here to work from home. The result has been a holiday atmosphere of sorts in a city with a tech sector known for its punishing “996” work schedules: 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week.

Youthful volunteers — mainly students at local universities — stand on street corners wearing bright red vests, having been offered academic credit in exchange for being trained as guides. Thousands of gawkers have been promenading past the large conference center that will host heads of state from across the Asia Pacific region, taking photos of themselves in front of the flower gardens inside the fence.

Among the crowds walking outside the high steel fences around the conference center was a local resident who had brought her parents and her dog. The resident noted that workers had been planting flowers for a year ahead of the summit, and added that a community worker had given her a massive package of napkins as a gift after she agreed not to drive her car in the coming week. Shenzhen has halved fares this week on its extensive subway system to help clear the roads for summit buses.

At the same time, however, residents are aware of occasional hassles. “Many friends who live around here plan to travel outside the city because of the inconvenience of transportation — many roads will be closed to traffic,” stated the resident, who gave only her family name, Zhang. As is common at high-profile and high-security events in China, she was wary of giving her full name, which can be risky for Chinese citizens.

Few dare to express any misgivings, however, accepting the disruption with resignation. “Even if we’re unhappy about it, we can’t really say so,” stated a resident surnamed Wang. “The government wouldn’t welcome our dissatisfaction.”.

It has been revealed that while gatherings of world leaders always prompt extensive security, China’s efforts in Shenzhen are particularly intensive. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous along streets in China and not noticeably more common this week in Shenzhen, but there are other, unobtrusive signs of the elaborate security effort underway.

Industry observers note that xiangmei Road, located near the main summit venue and lined with some of China’s costliest condominium towers, was much quieter than usual on Monday. A cleaner outside one of the towers who gave only her family name, Li, said that the family employing her has simply left town this week.

Police have been stationed in apartments on upper floors facing the conference center, drones have been prohibited and the remaining residents have received social media messages urging them to support the gathering, Ms. Li said.

“This place is usually very crowded,” she said, “but look how quiet it is now.”.

Exclusive: deal expected to be sealed in principle at EU-UK summit on Friday but trickier elements could be postponed for six months.

The new post-Brexit UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not come fully into force until 2030.

It will be a disappointment to any under-30s in the UK and the EU who hoped to travel, work or study in each other’s territories from next year after the long-awaited latest deal.

EU ambassadors will discuss the latest draft joint statement at a meeting on Wednesday in Brussels, with talk of youth mobility going right to the wire.

“We aim to apply this agreement no later than 2028 and endeavour to ensure that opportunities under the scheme will be available to our young people no later than January 2030,” a draft text agreed by negotiators from London and Brussels indicates.

The two sides aim to come to a “supplementary agreement” on tuition fees for EU citizens in UK universities.

The text on this most contentious subject is not yet agreed with two alternatives mooted in the draft text – either a deal that students pay a reduced international fee or, alternatively, the same fee as UK nationals. The aim is that this would be agreed separately within six months.

This is to allow linkage with the Made in Europe legislation that will not reach its final stages until possibly April next year in a vote in the European parliament. The legislation is designed to give priority to EU supply chains in the car and other industries.

By linking the two issues the UK can get assurances that the final detail of the deal on mobility cannot be signed off unless it has been included in the Made in Europe legislation.

EU countries including Germany could accept an unlimited number of young Britons under a youth mobility scheme, according to sources.

Fresh details on how a scheme might work have emerged with EU leaders and the UK expected to settle on a quota of about 100,000 a year being allowed to work, travel or study in each other’s territories.

The UK has insisted on a quota of EU citizens entering the UK under the scheme to guard against mass migration, but some countries have remarked they will not follow suit on the other side of the Channel and would be open to taking unlimited numbers.

The quota is expected to be worked out on a country-by-country basis with smaller countries such as Malta and Luxembourg seeking a system that will not be based on a per-capita quota per EU member state.

The new agrifood deal would not be agreed until 1 March 2028, the draft statement seen by the Guardian confirms.

In what looks to be a breakthrough for Burnham there may also be a commitment to enter a dialogue to remove barriers to touring artists, particularly bands and theatres companies that perform in multiple EU member states.

The 72-point joint statement also paves the way for further deals on steel between the UK and the EU.

But there is no agreement yet on whether the UK would commit to dynamically aligning with the EU on trade defence measures such as tariffs on Chinese cars.

The details came as Burnham remarked there is “no rush” to decide on the UK’s longer-term relationship with the EU, as he came under pressure from his own party to press the brakes on the pace of the rethink.

The prime minister said he would “take stock” of the wider relationship after Friday’s summit in Brussels, at which he also hopes to secure agreements on food and farming and emissions trading.

In an interview with Sky News, Burnham admitted he would now not set out the full options for a closer EU relationship until December – but denied he was “stepping back” from his previous commitments to pursue ties.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there's no question the PS5 has handed the Xbox Series X and S their collective rear ends from a sales perspective this console generation. That's a shame for Microsoft fans. Even though there are drawbacks you should understand before buying an Xbox Series X, for my money, it's still an excellent console. It's also one that supports a rich suite of accessibility options, as does its little sibling. One of the biggest? Fairly robust keyboard and mouse support.

Using traditional PC peripherals on a console might seem a bit outfield, but hey, the Dreamcast was doing it a quarter of a century ago, so there's definite precedent. There are actually a ton of Xbox games that offer at least partial mouse and keyboard support. Let's get into the mouse and keyboard options that should work with the Xbox Series X/S, and also discuss how to set them up. Plus, we'll examine just how many games support non-gamepad control schemes on Microsoft's current-gen consoles.

You sure can... but there are caveats. While Microsoft has done a commendable job at providing accessibility features for Xbox fans, mouse and keyboard support on Xbox Series X/S isn't universal across all games. Additionally, of the titles that do work with PC-based peripherals, not all of them offer native support. That means certain actions in non-native titles will require you to have a controller nearby to progress.

According to recent reports, there are more restrictions, too. There's at the moment no way to connect a Bluetooth mouse or keyboard to either Xbox Series console. For those looking to hook up their favorite PC gizmos, you're looking at either wired peripherals or ones that come with 2.4GHz dongles.

That's slightly annoying. The best Xbox Series X/S accessories are generally wireless because you're likely sitting a decent distance away from your TV while playing your favorite games. Unless you keep your Xbox at a desk like a PC, wired mice and keyboards are probably out of the question for everyday living room play. Dongles it is, then.

Sources indicate that oh, and there's one more catch. You can't use a mouse to navigate around the Xbox dashboard, which is a bit of a bummer.

Sources indicate that setting up a keyboard and mouse on an Xbox Series X/S is relatively simple, but functionality beyond that is going to vary based on the specific game. The easiest and most practical way to get started with PC peripherals on your Xbox is to plug in a wireless keyboard dongle and a mouse dongle: You can use the two USB-A slots on the back of either console, or the one at the front.

According to recent reports, from there, you can utilize the keyboard for typing on the Xbox dashboard (though as previously mentioned, mouse navigation is a no-go). Once you launch a game, things are a tad up in the air. The title may recognize your PC-style peripherals immediately, and you can start pointing and clicking. Or, you may well need your trusty Xbox controller to navigate into the settings menu, where you should be able to select mouse and keyboard inputs, if the title supports them. Microsoft provides the platform, but accessibility options are up to the individual developer, so this workflow will vary game to game.

In a recent development, basically, prepare to always have your gamepad in reach if you want to use typical PC peripherals with an Xbox Series console. Just in case.

Sources indicate that A surprising amount. We're not quite talking PC levels here, but the list of Xbox games with current mouse and keyboard support (as reported by Pure Xbox) shouldn't be sniffed at by WASD fans. Well over 100 titles feature levels of mouse and keyboard functionality at present, though native support isn't guaranteed in all of them. That means you'll occasionally have to break out your Xbox controller to navigate menus. If you hop on the Xbox Store, a game's listing page should tell you what level of mouse and keyboard support a title offers. Those that don't natively offer traditional PC controls will be marked as "Limited.".

In a recent development, looking for a few big hitters that support native mouse and keyboard controls on Xbox Series X/S? You'll find Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, Halo Infinite and Gears of War: E-Day. Considering one of those games demands complex simulation controls that never quite felt at home on a pad, and the other two involve landing headshots on alien beasties from afar, mouse and keyboard sounds like a great way to experience all three. I always thought Master Chief's 2021 open world was overly criticized, and now I'm eager to replay it on Xbox, sniping hordes of Brutes with my favorite mouse, the Inphic F9 Mecha.

There are also competitive shooters like Overwatch that support cross-platform play, and will automatically pair you with fellow mouse and keyboard users if the game detects a PC-style control scheme on console. After all, in a fast-paced online shooter, bringing a gamepad to a mouse-and-keyboard match is like wielding a pillow in a lightsaber battle.

There are a number of benefits to using desktop peripherals with an Xbox Series X/S. Some aren't all that sexy — oooh, I can type my custom license plate in Forza Horizon 6 a teeny bit quicker — but others have far more practical use cases.

Sources indicate that for simulation or strategy games with multiple mechanical layers and rich inventory systems, mouse and keyboard inputs are simply superior. I've had great experiences with these devices on my Xbox Series X playing Jurassic World Evolution 3, even though the dino-park management title does work pretty well with a controller. Keyboard support also gives you more quick buttons to assign should an Xbox title support it, which can definitely be useful in games that involve heavy inventory management, like Cyberpunk 2077.

The main reason you want keys and a mouse, though? For fans of first-person shooters, gamepads can never come close to the accuracy of blasting bullets with the utter precision of a mouse. Halo Infinite, Overwatch, the Call of Duty series and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl are all well-situated for mouse and keyboard play, among many other headshot-heavy games.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person stated, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”.

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have noted.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

It has been revealed that CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official stated in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”.

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, remarked at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”.

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

CNN’s Alex Marquardt contributed to this report.

  • A group representing industry bosses said it wants commitments from Andy Burnham and European political leaders that the restrictions will be one of the priorities in 2027 for furthering ties between the two sides, after a summit in Brussels this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CBI claims restrictions on cross-Channel work trips are hindering investment and trade between UK and Europe.

Business chiefs have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease Brexit restrictions on business travel for cross-Channel work trips.

A group representing industry bosses said it wants commitments from Andy Burnham and European political leaders that the restrictions will be one of the priorities in 2027 for furthering ties between the two sides, after a summit in Brussels this week.

The Confederation of British Industry (CBI), which represents some of Britain’s largest companies, welcomed the prime minister’s recent calls for a reset with Europe, designed to reverse some of the damage to Britain’s economy caused by Brexit.

But it mentioned Brexit restrictions, which include making employees obtain work permits for travel, are deterring cross-border investors and hampering trade at the very time both sides are trying to build resilience against China.

Sean McGuire, the CBI’s director of Europe and international, mentioned discussions should have been a priority in the talks this week, after a UK-EU summit in 2025 held by Keir Starmer also referenced improving business mobility.

It has been revealed that “Very little has been achieved. In fact, practically nothing has been achieved. The emphasis was put on youth mobility,” said McGuire.

EU diplomats have remarked in the past that the UK pushed hard for improving business mobility but was met with resistance from the bloc, where member states see British services – a substantial export particularly in the financial sector – as a threat.

McGuire said that energy, defence and car industry bosses say they are being hampered by the inability to travel freely in Europe to service or run multinational operations.

He said the issue should be of interest to all sides as they build on multiple existing laws to protect European supply chains.

“Now that we’ve got youth mobility potentially in the Friday deal, we should move seriously to address the kind of business mobility, which would apply to both the goods sector and the services sector,” he noted.

British citizens travelling to the EU post-Brexit are restricted to 90 days at a time out of a maximum of 180 days a year, limiting companies’ ability to promote employees and travel.

“If you are a CEO of a multinational you can very promptly clock up 90 days,” McGuire remarked.

Separately, work permits have to be obtained for each country that a worker travels to. That can affect the servicing of equipment, particularly in engineering, where products that cost millions such as lifts, escalators and factory machines come with service and maintenance contracts.

“There is a major difference between irregular migration, which needs to be tackled, and business mobility, which is bringing investment into the UK and vice versa,” he said.

While an agreement is close on youth mobility, Burnham faces the same roadblock when it comes to opportunities for under-30s, who will be offered a three-year visa scheme to work, travel or study.

“It is a trick because the UK is negotiating with Brussels but work permits are a national competency,” said one EU diplomat.

But McGuire stated there is a quick fix for business mobility, involving changes to the annex of the EU-UK trade and cooperation agreement, which allows the two sides to expand visa-free business travel across more industries without reworking the main treaty.

The CBI said it is also “disappointed” that no progress has been made on mutual recognition of qualifications allowing British or EU professionals to practise in each other’s territories as they did before Brexit.

Sources mentioned there was a view in Brussels that mutual recognition of qualifications was more beneficial to the UK than to the EU, causing energy around the talks to drain away.

The streamer has dropped an action-packed trailer that's filled to the brim with sci-fi setpieces and it looks pretty nifty.

For the uninitiated, 3 Body Problem was co-created by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss. Yes, those are the two guys who made Game of Thrones. Alexander Woo is also a co-creator and he wrote for programs like The Terror, True Blood and Wonderfalls.

The series is basically a hard sci-fi take on an alien invasion story spread across multiple generations. The first season certainly looked gorgeous and featured standout performances from Benedict Wong, Liam Cunningham and Rosalind Chao, among others.

We don't exactly know how the second season will handle some of the more narratively finicky aspects of the novel (no spoilers here.) Woo has always noted that the "guiding principle" of the series is to "retain the spirit" of the source books, so we'll have to wait and see.

It has been revealed that there is a spot of bad news here. The first season consisted of eight episodes, but the second includes just six. All six episodes were directed by Game of Thrones veterans Jeremy Podeswa and Miguel Sapochnik.

  • Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), ranking member of the House Natural Resources Committee, mentioned it is a “pivotal time” for US climate and energy policy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ANTALYA, Turkey—After their substantial gains in the 2026 midterm elections, a delegation of Democratic US House members appeared at the United Nations COP31 climate change conference Monday, pledging to rejoin the international fight against global warming.

Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), ranking member of the House Natural Resources Committee, mentioned it is a “pivotal time” for US climate and energy policy.

“The wrecking ball of Donald Trump and this out-of-touch administration, and the temporarily empty chair of the United States at this COP31, does not represent what the Americans want or need,” Huffman said.

In a recent development, president Donald Trump has pulled the United States out of the Paris climate agreement twice and is trying to quit the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The current administration has also tried to cut all funding for climate programs.

Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, the United States has had no formal government presence at the UN talks, but was informally represented by America Is All In, a coalition including local governments, businesses, faith groups, Native American tribes, and universities.

Huffman mentioned the midterm election reveals that Americans have rejected the current administration’s efforts to “turn the United States into something like a petro-dictatorship.” The results could pave the way for the country to reestablish a formal presence at the annual talks.

It has been revealed that given legal uncertainties about Trump’s efforts to completely withdraw the US from the UN’s climate framework, the extent of US participation in the talks is unclear. But Huffman remarked that, in the past, US congressional delegations have attended the annual Conference of the Parties, as the meeting is formally known, under both Democratic and Republican majorities.

“The next time we’re here, we will be an official congressional delegation led by the leadership of the House of Representatives,” Huffman noted in an interview with Inside Climate News.

The US would still be excluded from the formal government-to-government negotiations, but a congressional delegation representing the majority party, potentially capable of advancing climate and energy legislation, could make a difference, Huffman mentioned.

“We want to take the best practices that we’ve heard from all of the global partners… and craft them into good, solid climate policy once we get back to Congress,” remarked Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.).

In a recent development, the newly introduced Democratic majority in the House of Representatives can also use its oversight authority to try to ensure that the money the US has promised for climate aid and sustainable development is restored, said U.S. Rep. Sean Casten (D-Ill.).

Casten said some of America’s European allies are “spending $500, $600 million per day more than before the United States attacked Iran” because of increased oil prices, and that simply stopping those hostilities could free up funding for climate efforts.

Industry observers note that “We have lost [the] trust of the international community when it comes to climate,” mentioned Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.).

In a recent development, “I think it is a complete betrayal of our responsibility that Donald Trump has pulled us out of the Paris Agreement not once but twice,” she said. A Democrat winning the 2028 presidential election would help ensure the US can rejoin that agreement, she added.

It will take time to regain trust in the international community, Ansari remarked.

“But we will come back,” she said, “working 10 times harder, 50 times harder than we did before, to make sure that we are being team players, to make sure that we are… supporting small island developing states and supporting vulnerable African nations.”.

Climate activists reacted cautiously to the promises about the United States’ potential return to the international climate arena.

“We welcome the political shift in the United States that puts the brakes on the reckless dismantling of domestic green policies,” said Harjeet Singh, director of Satat Sampada Climate Foundation. “However, here at COP31 in Antalya, the international community cannot afford to celebrate prematurely or suffer from collective amnesia.”.

Singh said the US has a long history of obstructing climate negotiations across successive administrations and regardless of which party holds power.

Sources indicate that “As the world’s largest historical emitter, the US carries an outsized moral and legal responsibility to act,” he said. “Real change will not be measured by who walks through the halls of this summit, but by whether Washington finally ends its expansion of oil, gas, and coal at home and delivers hundreds of billions of dollars in grant-based climate finance to developing countries.”.

Singh mentioned until the US pays its fair share to help vulnerable countries recover from climate impacts and transition to sustainable energy systems, “warm words from visiting lawmakers mean very little to communities on the frontlines.”.

Brandon Wu, with ActionAid USA, said the new Democrat-led House majority must reassert control over the budget and hold the Trump administration accountable for “likely illegal actions like dismantling USAID and gutting foreign assistance” funding approved by Congress.

“What they can deliver to the United Nations process is extremely limited,” he remarked, adding that it’s unlikely there will be any sweeping newly introduced climate legislation or climate funding in the next two years. What members of Congress can do is lay the groundwork for more ambitious action in a post-Trump era, he added.

While meeting delegates from other countries, Huffman said he’s heard both gratitude and optimism, as well as skepticism, about a possible US return to the climate talks.

In a recent development, “The fact is the US has become kind of an unreliable partner and we’ve lost our credibility,” he remarked. “So we’ve tried to bring humility to this moment. We’ve got work to do to reclaim our credibility in this institution.”.

Bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species, and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News.

UK politics live – latest updates.

David Lammy has urged Andy Burnham to campaign on a promise to rejoin the EU at the next election.

The former foreign secretary, who also served as deputy prime minister under Keir Starmer, stated the prime minister’s Liverpool conference speech “blew the door wide open” on the issue.

It has been revealed that “Burnham’s Labour should go into the next election clear that its intention is to rejoin the EU,” Lammy wrote in the Times. “Forming the next government would give it the mandate to begin formal negotiations.

According to recent reports, “Once a deal is agreed, this should be put to the people. Unlike the last referendum, the public should have the opportunity to decide between two clearly defined choices.”.

His intervention comes as Burnham prepares for a major UK-EU summit in Brussels amid renewed scrutiny over Britain’s relationship with the bloc.

Sources indicate that the prime minister promised in his Labour conference speech in September that he would lay out different options to the country around the time of the November summit. But with the Brussels meeting approaching on Friday, Burnham appeared to prolong the timeline.

In a speech on Monday, he remarked he would start a discussion with the bloc on options after the summit, before presenting options to the public at a later date.

In a recent development, pressed on whether reopening the Brexit topic had become toxic, the Labour leader told Sky News on Tuesday: “I’m in a negotiation about improving the Brexit deal. That’s what I’m doing this week. We’ll see how it goes. And then we will consider whether there are options to further the relationship with the EU. And I’ll set that out later this year alongside the 10-year plan.

“But I don’t agree with you at all, actually, that it’s a toxic debate.”.

He repeated his pledge to stick to the 2024 Labour manifesto’s red lines – which rule out returning to the customs union, single market or free movement – before a general election and that the “British public will be in charge of whatever comes next”.

According to recent reports, he denied changing the timeframe he had laid out in September, saying: “I will set out next month what the next phase looks like. And that is exactly what I mentioned at my conference speech.”.

Burnham also launched an attack on the former Conservative prime minister Boris Johnson, who alongside David Cameron has cautioned him against returning to the bloc.

He also stated the youth guarantee scheme to get young people into work, which has formed part of the reset negotiations with the EU, would only be open to British citizens.

Concerns have been raised that the scheme to be agreed at the summit in Brussels on Friday, which could allow tens of thousands of young Europeans to work temporarily in the UK each year, and vice versa, could cut into fresh support for young Britons.

The former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn announced his recommendations for how to bring down the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) on Tuesday.

He remarked British young people should be the priority for hiring, whatever the outcome of the EU deal. The prime minister later told ITV’s Good Morning Britain he was looking to create “priority opportunities” for young people. He was asked if the jobs guarantee scheme, which aims to help 90,000 young people into work by March 2029, would exclude Europeans.

Recent findings suggest that he noted: “Yes, because we have a situation at the moment through the youth guarantee where employers receive a payment to take on somebody who’s been long-term unemployed. So that’s the scheme and we can, of course, design that scheme to support young British kids who are not in education, employment or training, and absolutely that will be the way we go forward.”.

#23879. Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Review: Furiously Fast but Flawed

Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Review: Furiously Fast but Flawed

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out.
  • Sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly.
  • In a recent development, the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out. This significant, boxy phone offers cutting-edge performance, long battery life, and a large display. You also get touch-sensitive shoulder buttons, RGB lighting, and gaming-focused software features.

Sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly. While this series has always been a clear bargain for gamers seeking the best chipset, it’s harder to swallow the compromises lurking here (camera, software, patch commitment) when the price starts at $949.

In a recent development, the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter. I’m a fan of the translucent industrial aesthetic and RGB lighting, but it’s not something I really want in my everyday phone. I had exactly the same issues with the 12 Pro as I had with the 10 Pro I reviewed two years ago. It’s very massive, so you really feel it in your pocket, and it can be awkward to handle, especially when you’re trying to scroll one-handed. It’s also the most slippery phone ever. Every time I put it down, the 12 Pro slowly starts to slide away.

Recent findings suggest that the big positive of this design is that it feels great in landscape orientation for gaming. The thick frame is easy to hold. There are touch-sensitive shoulder buttons on the top edge, and Nubia has a dedicated Magic Key for gaming mode, though you can customize it to launch the camera. This used to be a switch, but is now a red button. It’s still flanked by the round power button. Sadly, there’s no headphone port.

Recent findings suggest that it’s refreshing not to have a camera bump on the back, though this inevitably adds to the slipperiness, and this glass sandwich rapidly gets covered in finger smudges. Nubia has toned down the lighting a little, but you can still customize it for all sorts of activities. There’s a powerful cooling fan inside, with two vents to expel hot air, but the 12 Pro still somehow scores an IP68/69 rating for dust and water resistance.

The 6.85-inch OLED display is completely uninterrupted, with no notch or cutout camera to break it up. There’s an effective fingerprint sensor at the bottom and a less effective selfie camera under the top of the screen. The screen can hit a 185-Hz refresh rate, but only a handful of games actually support it. Most of the time you’ll be capped at 120 Hz. It supports HDR with 5,000-nit local peak brightness for highlights, but overall brightness is capped at 1,900 nits. Overall, it’s a lovely display, and a pleasure to play games or watch movies on. The Dolby Atmos–certified stereo speakers are decent for a phone.

Perhaps the biggest enticement is Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with Redmagic’s RedCore R5 chipset and 12 or 16 GB of RAM. You won’t find a faster Android phone right now, and the Redmagic 12 Pro can even give the iPhone 18 Pro a run for its money. Benchmark scores topped the Android charts, above phones like Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Industry observers note that I had no concerns playing Asphalt Legends and Wuthering Waves with settings cranked to the max. I also tried PUBG Mobile, one of the titles that can support that 185-Hz refresh rate, and it was smooth sailing. The 12 Pro keeps its cool, even after an hour or so of challenging gaming. Aside from the fan and vapor chamber for cooling, Nubia added dual-loop liquid cooling. You do get some fan noise and thermal throttling, but the 12 Pro has enough grunt to satisfy even the most hardcore of gamers.

In a recent development, to keep you gaming for longer, the 12 Pro boasts an enormous 8,400-mAh battery. Even with hours of gaming, I made it to the end of every day with something left in the tank. With careful use, you could easily push this phone to two days. There’s no charger in the box, but it supports up to 80-watt wired or wireless charging if you spring for a Redmagic charger. It took me an hour and 17 minutes to charge it from dead, but you can hit around 50 percent in half an hour. Sadly, it doesn’t support Qi2 magnets, so you’ll need a flat wireless charging pad.

To get top-notch performance at this price, you’ll have to accept several compromises. Let’s start with the camera. While the main 50-megapixel camera is quite good, and there’s a 50-megapixel ultrawide, the flat design doesn’t leave room for a telephoto lens, so you can only get 2X zoom by cropping. The main camera will satisfy folks who only snap the odd photo, and it does well in most conditions. The ultrawide is fine for group shots, but its smaller sensor means performance suffers in low light. The 16-megapixel front-facing camera is hidden under the screen, and it’s fine for video calls or well-lit selfies, though shots often look a bit muddy.

According to recent reports, the real problem with the 12 Pro’s camera is the processing. Use the terrible portrait mode or zoom in too far and you’ll see how badly it handles image processing. Nubia lacks Google’s expertise in this space, so a camera system that sounds similar on paper produces far worse photos in reality. Nubia’s colors often look a bit off, it really struggles with mixed lighting, and shots tend to be noisy or oversharpened. Video recording is quite good with the main camera, but stabilization was a little poor in some of the videos I shot.

Recent findings suggest that another big turnoff with the 12 Pro is the software. Redmagic OS 12 sits atop Android 17, and it’s mostly OK, though I wish Chinese manufacturers didn’t feel the need to imitate things like Apple’s Liquid Glass. The interface also has some bad translations. What’s worse is the prevalence of absolute junk bloatware and the subpar enhancement commitment. Nubia is only promising two years of platform updates and three years of security software updates in the US (five years in the UK).

Industry observers note that our best Android phones guide includes many more well-rounded options than the 12 Pro. You can even buy a Pixel 11 Pro XL on sale for the same price right now. But the 12 Pro is all about gaming, and to that end, it offers the best performance-and-screen combo you can get today. Whether the gaming features, cooling tech, and overall style add enough value depends on you. That same chipset will roll into more phones soon, and most of them will have a better camera and longer software support, but they’re likely to be more expensive, like the forthcoming Motorola Signature 27 at $1,600.

For buyers in the US, check your carrier bands. The 12 Pro should be fine with T-Mobile and its associated MVNOs, but it may not work well, or at all, with some other carriers. It also doesn’t support eSIM, so you need a physical SIM card. The 12-GB RAM and 256-GB storage model is $949; upgrading to 16 GB and 512 GB costs $1,049, and the 1-TB model is $1,199.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Make sure you're getting the most out of your Xbox Series X.
  • In a recent development, this sounds like an idiotic suggestion at first, right?
  • According to recent reports, though your current TV may support HDMI 2.1, the input that ensures the Series X can display its maximum resolution and framerate, that doesn't mean all of your TV's ports are 2.1 compliant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Make sure you're getting the most out of your Xbox Series X.

In a recent development, this sounds like an idiotic suggestion at first, right? Surely all you need to do is plug the HDMI cable that came with your Series X into your television, and you'll be ready to enjoy the best Xbox games, no? It's not always that simple.

According to recent reports, though your current TV may support HDMI 2.1, the input that ensures the Series X can display its maximum resolution and framerate, that doesn't mean all of your TV's ports are 2.1 compliant. This latest high-def standard really matters, as without it, cutting-edge visual features like Variable Refresh Rate are off the table.

It's important to know the specifics of your current TV. For instance, if it's an aging model that only supports HDMI 2.0, you can stop reading this article now, and content yourself with a top output of 1440p/120 fps or 4K/60 fps from your Series X. However, if you own a semi-modern budget flatscreen, there's a good chance only one or two of its ports will be compatible with HDMI 2.1, enabling 4K/120 fps and framerate-smoothing VRR from the Xbox.

Let's get to know your TV's HDMI sockets a little better, discuss whether you should upgrade the cable that came in the box with your Series X, and go over why HDMI 2.1 is so important for current-gen gaming.

It has been revealed that possibly, but it's entirely dependent on the model of TV you own. If you picked up your screen within the last five years and it wasn't an ultra-budget panel, it probably supports HDMI 2.1. But remember, even with a newish TV, there's no guarantee that all of its ports are HDMI 2.1 compatible.

Most modern high-end sets will have three to four HDMI 2.1 ports total, so if you've bought a premium OLED or MicroLED panel in the last couple of years, it's likely that all of its HDMI inputs will comply. If your set is a good few years old and was one of the first models to support HDMI 2.1 features, there's a decent chance that only one of its ports can take advantage of the Xbox Series X's 4K/120 max output.

In a recent development, to assess your TV's port situation without any awkward bending or flashlight usage, check out your model's online manual. Otherwise, individual inputs tend to be labeled on the backside of the TV itself. My 2023 LG OLED has four HDMI 2.1 ports, so thankfully I never have to worry about connection complications, but it's often the case that certain brands and less-recent models favor HDMI 2.1 in specific slots. Take Sony as an example: Older Bravia displays usually reserve their 2.1 configurations to ports three and four. Again, it entirely depends on your specific model. And when in doubt, reference your TV's online manual.

Industry observers note that in the vast majority of circumstances, you should definitely not replace the Ultra High Speed HDMI cable that came in the box with your beloved Microsoft machine. That puppy is fully HDMI 2.1 compliant   and it's likely to have a far greater shelf life than any Xbox Series X. For most folks, there really is no reason to upgrade the Series X's standard cable. Of course, there are exceptions.

In a recent development, depending on the logistics of your gaming setup, you might need a longer HDMI cable than the one Microsoft provides. It's 6 feet long, which will be plenty for most Xbox players. But if for some reason you can't place your Series X as close to the TV as you'd like, investing in a lengthier cable might be worthwhile. Just make sure it's HDMI 2.1 certified and you're good to go.

It has been revealed that there's also the case for folks who wall-mount their TVs. I can personally attest that getting the Xbox's HDMI 2.1 cable into one of my LG G3 OLED's outputs was a nightmare, as my screen is flush to the wall. In these instances, it's definitely worth investing in an HDMI cable with an ultra-thin connector. Again, just check that it's HDMI 2.1 compliant.

Please, please never been suckered into buying a "premium" HDMI cable. That word is basically a money-grabbing marketing tool used to lure in impulsive AV enthusiasts. I should know: I still have a painful memory of being sweet-talked into purchasing a $75 HDMI cable back in 2015, right after picking up my first OLED TV. Trust me, the ultra-fast cable that came with your Xbox Series X will do just fine.

There are actually a surprising number of games that can hit 120 fps on the Xbox Series X (and even its smaller sibling, the Series S), as noted by Pure Xbox. The massive caveat? Few Xbox games can run at such a high framerate while also outputting at 4K resolution. Last-gen titles that got Series X upgrades like Halo: The Master Chief Collection can output at a full-fat 4K/120, but even popular first-party games like Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, Forza Horizon 6 and Doom the Dark Ages are locked at 60 fps on the console.

In a recent development, otherwise, the Series X often hits 120 fps with an associated drop in resolution. Pretty much every modern Call of Duty installment supports 120 fps, from Black Ops Cold War right up to this year's Modern Warfare 4. The catch? Dynamic resolution is usually deployed, often dropping in-game clarity to either 1080p or 1400p. If you want faster framerates on Series X, in most cases you're going to have to accept a dip in resolution.

There are drawbacks you should know about before buying an Xbox Series X, but when push comes to shove, its visual output really boils down to having a proper HDMI cable, and the age and manufacturer of the connected display. To get the most out of your Xbox Series X, start by making sure your HDMI 2.1 ports and cables are in order.

Labour faces double blow over UK fossil fuel projects

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Massive North Sea operator EnQuest says it is quitting oil basin, while SSE threatens to close Yorkshire gas storage site.
  • The energy secretary has been dealt a double blow after two UK companies signalled plans to pull their investment from a series of major fossil fuel projects over government policies.
  • One of the North Sea’s biggest independent companies, EnQuest, said on Wednesday it was quitting the oil basin to focus on making better returns in Asia, blaming the “uncertain investment environment within the UK”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Massive North Sea operator EnQuest says it is quitting oil basin, while SSE threatens to close Yorkshire gas storage site.

The energy secretary has been dealt a double blow after two UK companies signalled plans to pull their investment from a series of major fossil fuel projects over government policies.

One of the North Sea’s biggest independent companies, EnQuest, said on Wednesday it was quitting the oil basin to focus on making better returns in Asia, blaming the “uncertain investment environment within the UK”.

Separately, the energy tech giant SSE told investors that next summer it would close one of the country’s largest gas storage sites, which is on the North Sea coast, unless the government intervened to offer support amid weak market conditions.

The tacit criticism is expected to pile pressure on Miatta Fahnbulleh, who became the energy secretary in July, to clarify the government’s strategy to secure the UK’s gas supplies as households face a rise in energy bills this winter because of soaring gas costs.

EnQuest set out prepares to sell its entire portfolio of UK oilfields to the biggest North Sea producer, Neo Next+, for up to $960m (£730m), weeks after the organization urged the chancellor, John Healey, to use his budget in November to reform the industry’s tax regime.

The UK oil and gas industry warned after the budget that the Treasury’s decision to leave its planned North Sea tax changes until the end of the decade was “continuing to drive energy investment abroad”.

The British oil organization BP is also in the process of exiting the North Sea after announcing in the summer that it would end six decades of production from the basin by selling its entire business there.

Industry observers note that the EnQuest deal marks “another significant tech giant exiting the UK continental shelf”, according to James Hosie, an equity analyst at Shore Capital. He mentioned the company had opted to leave after 16 years as a leading independent operator in the basin “rather than hold out for an improvement in the UK regulatory and fiscal regime for upstream oil and gas”.

SSE told investors that while its Atwick gas storage site in the north of England had a “strategic importance” to the energy system as the North Sea’s domestic production declined, it was “increasingly clear that existing market arrangements do not support their continued operation”.

Closing the Atwick facility, near Hornsea on the East Yorkshire coast, would remove about 309m cubic metres of gas, or about 1.5 days’ worth of Great Britain’s gas usage, from the UK’s storage capacity.

The site makes up a fifth of the country’s onshore gas storage capacity, or 7% when including the storage tanks at the UK’s liquified natural gas terminals and the Rough site, also at risk of closure unless its owner, Centrica, the parent tech giant of British Gas, can agree a long-term financial support deal with the government.

The renewed concerns over supplies emerged on the same day that the National Energy System Operator (Neso) warned in a second consecutive annual report that the UK was at risk of a gas supply crisis as the North Sea’s production winds down.

Sources indicate that the report echoed concerns that while the UK has enough access to global gas markets to cover demand when weather is normal, if even a single piece of Britain’s ageing gas infrastructure suffered an “unlikely” outage during a very cold spell, then supplies could fall short of demand. This would lead to emergency measures such as shutting off gas supplies to factories, power plants and – in extreme scenarios – homes.

Energy companies typically rely on stockpiling gas in their storage facilities during the summer, when prices are usually lower because of weaker demand, before selling the gas at a profit during winter when demand for energy usually lifts market prices.

However, the gas price increases triggered by the Iran conflict this year and by Russia’s war on Ukraine in 2022 has upended normal market patterns, leading to historic market price highs during the summer that have made it uneconomical to stockpile gas ahead of winter.

As a result, countries across Europe have entered the cooler months of the year with gas stores at their lowest level in more than a decade.

Sources indicate that britain already stores less gas than some of its European neighbours and is instead more reliant on liquefied natural gas imports. The closure of a storage facility such as Atwick could leave the UK even more exposed to price shocks on global markets.

Last month, Fahnbulleh gave the final approval for the Jackdaw gasfield, which began producing gas for the first time earlier this week. She is expected to make a decision on whether to consent to oil production from the Rosebank field before the end of the year.

The government was approached for comment.
