According to recent reports, shenzhen, China10:47 p.m. Nov. 18.

Peter BakerLily KuoPaul SonneKeith Bradsher and Leo Sands.

Peter Baker, Paul Sonne and Keith Bradsher reported from Shenzhen, China. Lily Kuo reported from Taipei, Taiwan. Leo Sands reported from London.

President Trump, Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir V. Putin of Russia greeted each other with smiles and handshakes on Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, hours after Mr. Trump received a personal welcome from Mr. Xi at the Chinese city’s airport that included a hug.

Industry observers note that the shows of friendliness by the three world leaders, on the eve of a trilateral summit, contrasted sharply with their divergent stances on some of the world’s most pressing concerns, including nuclear arms control, China’s ability to access advanced A.I. chips and the future of the war in Ukraine.

Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, the presidents are expected to participate in the first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, when at least some of those problems could be on the agenda. The summit will cap Mr. Trump’s whirlwind trip to Asia, which has been shadowed by the Nvidia scandal, trade conflicts and critical infrastructure breakdowns at home.

According to recent reports, earlier, Mr. Xi met Mr. Trump at the airport in Shenzhen, something he did not do when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. But Mr. Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Mr. Xi in September, an uncommon move for an American president and the first time Mr. Trump had done so for a foreign visitor. In effect, Mr. Xi returned the gesture.

The red-carpet greeting on the tarmac — with a crowd of people in colorful costumes waving flags and flowers and chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin — came shortly after Mr. Xi met with Mr. Putin, who arrived earlier in the day. The Chinese leader had sent a lower-ranking official to greet Mr. Putin but used their subsequent meeting to hail the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”.

The two encounters underscored Mr. Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States. While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have developed a bond, China has a far more extensive economic relationship with the United States.

Industry observers note that mr. Trump will also meet separately with Mr. Xi on Thursday, his third encounter this year with the Chinese leader after he visited Beijing in the spring and the lavish state visit at the White House a couple months ago. Although Mr. Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent on forging friendly ties between the world’s two largest economies.

The visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Mr. Trump has stated he does not intend to raise concerns of Chinese interference in American affairs. The chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign last week after revelations of an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence determined was spying for China. But Mr. Trump has said he will not discuss the matter with Mr. Xi.

Here’s what else we’re covering:.

According to recent reports, manila stop: Mr. Trump’s Asia tour began in Manila, where he joined a meeting of Southeast Asian nations. He also met with an old friend, Imelda Marcos, the former first lady of the Philippines and the mother of the country’s current president. Read more ›.

Canada: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said he had met with Mr. Trump on Wednesday in Shenzhen to discuss their countries’ trade dispute. Mr. Carney’s office said that the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement” but offered no further details.

Sources indicate that russian show of force: Russian strategic nuclear bombers landed in Vietnam around when Mr. Putin landed in China, an apparent signal before the trilateral talks with Mr. Trump that Moscow remained the world’s largest nuclear power. Read more ›.

Fast-food diplomacy: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines noted he had fried chicken from Jollibee, a chain that is considered a national treasure, delivered to Mr. Trump during his overnight stay in Manila. Read more ›.

According to recent reports, president Vladimir V. Putin of Russia held talks for more than two hours with China’s leader, Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before the two leaders were scheduled to meet with President Trump.

Sources indicate that as Mr. Putin landed in China, Russia engaged in a purposeful show of force by flying strategic nuclear bombers to Vietnam for the first time since the Soviet era. Mr. Putin spent much of the day demonstrating that despite his isolation from many Western nations over their opposition to the war in Ukraine, he remains on good terms with much of the rest of the world.

Mr. Xi greeted Mr. Trump at the airport when the American president arrived in Shenzhen, the first time he has greeted a foreign dignitary on the tarmac in more than a decade as China’s leader. In contrast, Mr. Xi sent a longtime deputy, Cai Qi, to welcome Mr. Putin, who arrived in the early hours of the morning.

Sources indicate that by arriving before Mr. Trump, Mr. Putin got extra face time with Asian leaders ahead of the scheduled trilateral meeting on Thursday between the United States, China and Russia. That meeting will be the first involving the leaders of those three countries.

Industry observers note that no relationship has proved more critical for Mr. Putin than his bond with Mr. Xi. Mr. Putin met with the Chinese leader for at least the fourth time this year on Wednesday, holding large group talks with the Russian and Chinese delegations in Shenzhen before moving on to a smaller “working breakfast” with top aides.

As a major purchaser of Russian energy and supplier of electronics and consumer goods, China has served as a lifeline for wartime Russia. Western companies pulled out of the Russian market after the invasion, and Moscow scrambled to adapt in the face of heavy sanctions.

At the outset of the talks with Mr. Xi, Mr. Putin underscored the rapidly increasing cooperation between Russia and China, noting that tourist flows had increased 43 percent since the countries introduced visa-free travel late last year.

Mr. Putin said both Russia and China were taking “constructive approaches to shaping a more equitable, multipolar world order.” That is the Russian leader’s favored oblique terminology for a world no longer dominated by the United States.

Sources indicate that mr. Putin also met with Vietnam’s leaders before joining a dinner at the summit, where he was welcomed by Mr. Xi and shook Mr. Trump’s hand.

The scheduled trilateral meeting comes as Moscow continues to play hardball with the Trump administration over talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.

Industry observers note that mr. Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff last week sought Mr. Putin’s approval to add European officials to talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, but the Kremlin rebuffed the request in public comments after the meeting.

Recent findings suggest that outside the trilateral meeting, it was not immediately clear how extensive talks between Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin would be. The Kremlin spokesman, Dmitri S. Peskov, told state news media that there most likely would not be time for full-fledged talks between Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin but said they would find time to discuss Ukraine and possibly Iran.

Sources indicate that at the banquet, President Trump was seated with his back to reporters at the center of the table and Xi Jinping on his left. When reporters were ushered out, the two leaders were conversing through interpreters.

About an hour later, the president departed and returned to his hotel for the night.

Recent findings suggest that president Trump, President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia and Xi Jinping, the leader of China, shook hands before the start of a banquet that includes the national leaders of the APEC summit. Trump, Putin and Xi proposal to hold a trilateral summit on Thursday.

Industry observers note that xi Jinping, standing at a podium adorned by flowers, lifted a glass of red wine and made a toast at the gathering of leaders. With so many visitors, roads are closed in many places across central Shenzhen.

Recent findings suggest that amid a bitter trade war between their countries, President Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney met in-person on the sidelines of the APEC summit for the first time since last year. In a statement, Mr. Carney’s office said that the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement” but offered no further details.

Unlike Trump, Putin was not greeted at the airport by Xi when he arrived in the middle of the night. Cai Qi, Xi’s longtime deputy, met the Russian leader.

According to recent reports, javier C. Hernández and Kiuko Notoya.

Industry observers note that the atmosphere was tense. The handshake was quick.

President Xi Jinping of China and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan met briefly on Wednesday at the opening of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, their first encounter since the start of a bitter diplomatic feud a year ago.

Sources indicate that mr. Xi offered Ms. Takaichi a slight smile as she made her way to a banquet with other world leaders. He did not appear to respond when she remarked a few words to him, before they posed for a photo with Mr. Xi’s wife, Peng Liyuan.

Sources indicate that experts remarked the interaction was unlikely to signify any serious thaw in relations, which have been at a low point since China reacted furiously last year to a comment Ms. Takaichi made about Taiwan.

Sources indicate that tetsuo Kotani, a professor at Meikai University in Chiba Prefecture in Japan, said that Ms. Takaichi seemed “eager to make the most of this opportunity” in Shenzhen. Mr. Xi, he said, “maintained a businesslike demeanor.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t think there’s any hope this time around for improved relations,” Mr. Kotani said.

As the summit got underway, there were reminders of the frosty state of relations. While other world leaders received warm welcomes at the Shenzhen airport — a crowd of dancing young people with flowers greeted the South Korean leader, for example — there were no such gestures for Ms. Takaichi, according to Japanese news reports.

The dispute began last year, when Ms. Takaichi, a longtime critic of China, told Japan’s Parliament that any attempt by Beijing to blockade or seize Taiwan could constitute a “survival-threatening situation” for Japan, implying a potential military response. Beijing considers Taiwan, a self-governed democracy, part of its territory.

Industry observers note that china unleashed a wave of reprisals against Japan, urging tourists to avoid the country, limiting the export of critical minerals and restricting Japanese seafood imports. At the same time, Chinese officials and commentators have hardened the language they use to describe Japan, with some seeking to belittle Ms. Takaichi by omitting her title in official settings.

China’s punishments have started to squeeze Japan. The decline in tourism has hurt sales at some duty-free stores, hotels and restaurants. Japan could soon run low on supplies of some rare earths — minerals used to make a range of essential technologies, from M.R.I. machines to drones — according to analysts.

Recent findings suggest that chinese officials and scholars have suggested that anything short of Ms. Takaichi retracting her comment on Taiwan would not satisfy Mr. Xi.

Sources indicate that shao Yuqun, director of the Institute for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said that Mr. Xi was responding in part to intense anger among the Chinese public over Ms. Takaichi’s remark.

Industry observers note that ms. Shao added that finding a way to improve relations with Japan was “certainly not the priority” in Shenzhen.

Sources indicate that ms. Takaichi has been working to accelerate Japan’s defense buildup to counter a volatile security environment, including threats from China, North Korea and Russia.

Sources indicate that there is little appetite among the Japanese public to curry favor with Beijing and Ms. Takaichi is unlikely to give in to Chinese demands to retract her remark on Taiwan. As she enters her second year in office, she enjoys relatively robust public support, and won a historic supermajority in the lower house of Japan’s bicameral Parliament in February.

The meeting had echoes of an encounter in 2014, when Mr. Xi offered an icy handshake to Shinzo Abe — then Japan’s prime minister and a mentor to Ms. Takaichi — at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing during another moment of tension between the two countries. Mr. Abe was eventually able to get more time with Mr. Xi, and relations between the two countries improved somewhat.

According to recent reports, after their encounter on Wednesday, Mr. Xi and Ms. Takaichi are unlikely to have an extended meeting in Shenzhen, officials from both countries said.

Sources indicate that ms. Takaichi is expected to face another challenge on Thursday: a potential sit-down on the sidelines of the summit with Russia’s president, Vladimir V. Putin. The meeting would take place as Mr. Putin is escalating pressure on Japan. He recently seized Russian assets of Japan Tobacco, detained a Japanese journalist and visited islands claimed by both Moscow and Tokyo.

Japan will also be watching the outcome of a first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.

Tobias Harris, the founder of the advisory firm Japan Foresight, said Tokyo hopes the meeting is “light on substance.”.

“You can’t rule out the eventual possibility of some attempts at a significant grand settlement that is prejudicial to the global order that Japan prefers,” he said.

Verena HölzlAie Balagtas See and Jason Gutierrez.

What President Trump appeared to lack in enthusiasm, his hosts in the Philippines made up for in hospitality by catering to his preferences during a brief state visit.

The president stopped in Manila on his way to a historic meeting with the autocratic leaders of Russia and China in Shenzhen, just as the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, was wrapping up.

He did not even go to the summit venue; Southeast Asian leaders met him at the hotel where he was staying.

Recent findings suggest that when President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines rushed to leave a news conference after wrapping up the ASEAN summit, he told reporters: “I cannot keep the president of the United States waiting. Sorry.”.

Recent findings suggest that for Mr. Marcos and much of the region, flattering Mr. Trump is part of a strategy of balancing the United States and China.

Recent findings suggest that although Mr. Marcos has called for a reset of relations with China, tensions remain high with Beijing over territorial claims in the South China Sea.

“Whether they like it or not, the Philippines is a traditional U.S. ally,” mentioned Georgi Engelbrecht, a Philippines analyst at the International Crisis Group, a think tank. “China will never trust it strategically.”.

The Philippines and the United States are bound by a 75-year-old mutual defense treaty.

In remarks before their bilateral meeting on Wednesday, Mr. Marcos seemed to make an effort to use language that would please his guest, referring to A.I. as “super intelligence,” a term Mr. Trump has made mandatory for his government.

Tapping into Mr. Trump’s predilection for fast food, Mr. Marcos said he had sent Mr. Trump fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee. “It’s providing extra energy for all the work that is in front of you,” Mr. Marcos said to the president at their meeting the next day.

Industry observers note that during his roughly three-minute speech, Mr. Marcos brought up Mr. Trump’s “brief stop” in Manila at least six times.

According to recent reports, for his part, Mr. Trump was also complimentary, telling Mr. Marcos that he was well acquainted with his parents, the dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos and his wife, Imelda Marcos, who came to be known for her shoe collection and unexplained wealth.

“You have very good genetics, I can tell you that,” Mr. Trump told Mr. Marcos at a dinner with Southeast Asian leaders on Tuesday.

“Personal chemistry and rapport between leaders is important,” said Lucio Pitlo III, the president of ThinkSea Consulting, a Philippine think tank. “But leveraging them to tangibly advance national interests is the more crucial metric.”.

In a recent development, he mentioned Mr. Marcos’s efforts to have good relations with Mr. Trump had paid off in the past, for example, in a proposed U.S. tariff rate that was half as much as in other parts of the region.

According to recent reports, filipinos have traditionally viewed the United States, its former colonial ruler, more favorably than they view China. But punishing tariffs and higher fuel prices as a result of the war in Iran have been difficult for the country to absorb.

It has been revealed that after his meeting with Mr. Marcos, Mr. Trump declared that the two sides had signed “a very big ⁠trade deal.” Mr. Marcos’s office described it a an “understanding on key areas of economic cooperation.”.

Industry observers note that personal diplomacy was on display again later in the day. Mr. Trump briefly spoke with Imelda Marcos, 97, who is now rarely seen in public. As he left, she blew him a kiss from her wheelchair.

Sources indicate that xi Jinping told President Trump that he took the unusual move for a Chinese leader of greeting him at the airport because the American president had done the same for him when he visited the United States in September. “China is a nation of etiquette with a tradition of reciprocity,” Xi said, according to Chinese state media.

Recent findings suggest that president Trump is arriving at the summit as his envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, face headwinds in trying to negotiate a peace deal with Russia to end the war in Ukraine. Kushner and Witkoff went to Moscow last week to seek Putin’s approval to add the Europeans to talks, but Kremlin officials publicly rebuffed the request.

Putin’s arrival was accompanied by the same orchestra playing the trepak, or Russian dance melody, from Pyotr Tchaikovsky’s “The Nutcracker.”.

Xi Jinping, the Chinese leader, welcomed guests in Shenzhen, where President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia arrived and shook hands with President Trump.

President Trump walked into the event on a red carpet as a Chinese orchestra played a rendition of “America the Beautiful.”.

Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada has advanced his goal of reducing Canada’s economic reliance on the United States during a weeklong swing through Asia, emerging with trade deals with China and the Philippines.

But he was also presented with an unexpected opportunity to improve relations with Washington. On Wednesday, Mr. Carney unveiled that he would meet with President Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, leaving open the prospect of Canada starting to mend the rift with its neighbor.

“We have long said, and believed and still believe, that there is a mutually beneficial agreement between Canada and the United States in the context of the fresh U.S. trade policy,” Mr. Carney told reporters. “We’ll have discussions on that. And, we will do what’s necessary in order to achieve that deal, but only if that deal that is in the interest of Canadians.”.

It has been revealed that hours later, Mr. Carney’s office issued a brief statement confirming that the two leaders met and “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement.” It offered no details.

Sources indicate that before Wednesday, Mr. Carney’s aides mentioned there was no expectation of a meeting with Mr. Trump in China. At the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in South Korea last year, the two men only spoke informally during a dinner.

Industry observers note that how much progress, if any, will result from the meeting is unclear. Before the encounter, Mr. Carney described dealing with the Trump administration on trade as a “two steps forward, one step back type thing.”.

Since his return to office, Mr. Trump has imposed a variety of tariffs on a wide range of Canadian products. While those tariffs have been effectively suspended for many goods that qualify as being made in North America, the suspension has not applied to the key auto, steel and aluminum industries. Their products face tariffs of up to 50 percent.

Negotiations between the two countries collapsed in August with each side pointing fingers at the other for the failure.

At the beginning of this month, Mr. Carney noted that talks would restart after Mr. Trump said the United States would back off on some secondary challenges that were irritants for Canada, including requirements relating to the promotion of Canadian and French language content on digital streaming services.

There has been little apparent activity since then but Mr. Carney said on Wednesday that “we have been making progress.”.

Industry observers note that much more obvious has been the progress Mr. Carney has made with China. Before he took office, diplomatic incidents — including what was widely seen in Canada as the hostage-taking of two Canadians by China in 2018 — and Canada’s decision to follow the United States with 100 percent tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles had brought relations between the two countries to a near standstill.

Industry observers note that but this week, at his second formal meeting with President Xi Jinping of China this year, Mr. Carney walked away with a second reduction in Chinese tariffs aimed at a variety of farm and fish products. The deal effectively marked the end of the trade war sparked by the auto tariff, Mr. Carney said, opening the door to an expanded trade relationship between the countries.

Mr. Carney also repeated this week that if Canada were unable to persuade Mr. Trump to end tariffs on its auto exports, it would look to China, Japan and Europe to keep Canada’s auto industry afloat.

Industry observers note that that suggestion drew criticism from Peter Navarro, a senior adviser to Mr. Trump.

“Are u really threatening to play China off the U.S.?” Mr. Navarro said in a social media post. “This is offensive in the extreme. You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive — as it is already doing.” Pete Hoekstra, Washington’s ambassador to Canada who has frequently offended Canadians, shared the post.

On Wednesday, however, Mr. Carney dismissed suggestions that Canada’s renewed relationship with China was poisoning its economically vital relationship with the United States.

“In my conversations with the president, he’s tried to understand where we are with China, where we’re going with China,” Mr. Carney said. “I shouldn’t speak for him, but in his hierarchy of problems, it’s not the top problem at all.”.

Sources indicate that but selling the benefits of China back home may not be so easy. A recent poll found that only 14 percent of Canadians want closer trade ties with China. By contrast, 58 percent back Mr. Carney’s push for a closer relationship with the European Union.

In a recent development, after noting that Canadian fishermen and farmers strongly favor more trade with China, Mr. Carney downplayed the extent of the trade relationship.

“Relative to many other countries, our trade with China is quite modest and the breadth of it is quite modest.”.

It has been revealed that yuri Ushakov, a top aide to President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, told Russian state news media that Putin may speak with President Trump at a dinner for leaders in Shenzhen this evening before their formal meeting on Thursday.

When President Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi Jinping was waiting for him at the bottom of the steps descending from Air Force One.

According to recent reports, it was the first time that Mr. Xi had personally received a foreign dignitary at the airport in more than a decade as China’s leader. Visiting leaders are usually welcomed by senior Chinese officials and greeted by Mr. Xi at the Great Hall of the People in central Beijing.

Mr. Xi’s appearance, while unusual, was likely about reciprocating Mr. Trump’s hospitality. When Mr. Xi traveled to Washington for a state visit in September, Mr. Trump greeted the Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews. That was the first time the U.S. president had personally greeted a foreign visitor upon their arrival.

Recent findings suggest that after Air Force One landed in Shenzhen for the last stop on his whirlwind trip to Asia, Mr. Xi rolled up to the tarmac in a black luxury sedan made by the Chinese carmaker Hongqi, or Red Flag. He walked toward the president’s plane along a red carpet flanked by young men and women cheering and waving American and Chinese flags. After Mr. Trump walked down the stairs from his plane toward Mr. Xi, the two shook hands. Mr. Trump patted Mr. Xi on the back before the two embraced.

Wu Xinbo, the dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai, mentioned the leaders’ personal receptions reflected a shift in the U.S.-China relationship to focus on “respect, fairness, and reciprocity.”.

Mr. Wu mentioned that Mr. Xi’s presence was also likely a message of support for the American president, to show that China will “still treat him seriously and would like to continue to work with him,” after the Republican Party suffered a bruising defeat in the recent midterm elections.

Recent findings suggest that the high-level reception accorded to Mr. Trump was a step up from the welcome given to President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, who arrived earlier on Wednesday. Mr. Putin was greeted by Cai Qi, a longtime deputy of Mr. Xi and one of the most influential officials in the Chinese leader’s inner circle. Industry observers note that when Mr. Trump visited China in May, he was greeted by China’s vice president, Han Zheng, a ceremonial figurehead who often attends formal diplomatic events. When he visited in 2017, the president was greeted by Yang Jiechi, China’s then-top diplomat and a member of the Politburo, the party’s second-most powerful body.

In 2009, when Mr. Xi was vice president and already seen as the likely successor to China’s leader at the time, Hu Jintao, Mr. Xi waited at the airport to greet President Barack Obama on his arrival in Beijing.

David Pierson contributed reporting from Hong Kong.

Paul Sonne reported from Shenzhen, China, and Damien Cave reported from Ho Chi Minh City.

President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

Mr. Putin arrived early Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, for a regional economic meeting and a trilateral summit with President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China. Satellite images indicated that two Russian Tu-95MS strategic nuclear bombers had landed on Tuesday at Da Nang Airport in nearby Vietnam alongside two long-range transport aircraft.

It was the first time that Russian strategic nuclear bombers had deployed to Vietnam since the Soviet era, a pointed demonstration of Russia’s nuclear might and global reach ahead of the high-level talks.

The surprise arrival of the Russian aircraft in the region caused a scramble among American allies in Asia.

According to recent reports, japan dispatched jets after Russian planes were detected in Japanese airspace near Okinoshima, an island in the south of Japan, and Tokyo registered its discontent with the Russian authorities. Recent findings suggest that but the one critical area where Russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Russia has also developed a range of fresh nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

In a recent development, the Tu-95MS is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

It has been revealed that taiwan on Tuesday said it detected two sorties of Russian military aircraft flying in airspace east of the island. Gen. Huang Chih-wei, the Vice Chief of the Taiwanese military’s General Staff, said that “the actions of the Russian aircraft undermine regional peace and stability and are detrimental to maintaining the status quo of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.”.

The Russian and Vietnamese authorities did not make any public statements about the arrival of the bombers. Mr. Putin met with Vietnam’s leader, To Lam, in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi are also attending.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

For Vietnam, the decision to welcome the Russian nuclear bombers highlights China that Vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by Beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.

But it is a careful balancing act for the Vietnamese.

Vietnam allowed Russia to refuel its bombers from Cam Ranh Bay in 2014 as they patrolled the area around Guam, but the refueling was done midair and the bombers did not land on Vietnamese soil. In a recent development, when Imelda Marcos and Donald J. Trump partied in New York in the 1990s, she was the exiled former first lady of the Philippines, the wife of an ousted dictator, and he was a real estate mogul facing multiple bankruptcies.

They met again in Manila on Wednesday in vastly different roles. Mr. Trump, 80, is, of course, the president of the United States. And Ms. Marcos, 97, is the mother of the president of the Philippines, her family ensconced again in Malacañang Palace.

Ms. Marcos wielded immense power when her husband was president and came to be known for her flamboyant lifestyle, shoe collection and unexplained wealth.

Industry observers note that “Since you’re strapped for time, I thought a taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late night snack for you and your delegation,” Mr. Marcos mentioned in his remarks before a meeting with Mr. Trump.

It has been revealed that mr. Marcos told Mr. Trump on Wednesday that Jollibee had surpassed Kentucky Fried Chicken in popularity in the United States. The claim was dubious but Mr. Trump replied: “Oh, wow, fantastic.”.

While KFC still has many more stores than Jollibee in the United States, the Filipino chain has promoted its fried chicken as America’s best since at least 2022, citing food critics’ rankings and three consecutive wins in a USA Today readers’ poll.

Sources indicate that on its home turf, Jollibee far outpaces American fast-food chains in store count and revenue. To compete with Jollibee in the Philippines, McDonald’s has altered its local menu to offer a sweeter hamburger sauce, fried chicken and rice, and Filipino-style sweet spaghetti.

Jollibee has expanded beyond the Philippines by acquiring food brands in countries such as the United States, China and South Korea, including the Colorado-based burger chain Smashburger and the Hong Kong dim sum chain Tim Ho Wan.

Mr. Marcos’s shout-out came as Jollibee is exploring a Hong Kong Stock Exchange listing for its international business, after initially saying it would list in the United States. In a recent development, jollibee has not opened any stores in Washington, though there are several in Upcoming York, Mr. Trump’s home state, and Florida, where he spends a lot of time.

Sources indicate that xi mentioned in a meeting with Putin that relations between China and Russia have remained as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain,” according to Chinese state media. Recent findings suggest that at a lunch with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines on Wednesday, Trump said that the two countries had unexpectedly signed a new trade deal. China warned on Tuesday that it could hit back after the Trump administration this week proposed a rule that would restrict China’s access to advanced chips through data centers outside its borders.

Putin and his team held talks with Xi followed by a smaller working breakfast. They have met dozens of times; this is at least their fourth in-person meeting this year. The talks lasted more than two hours, according to the Russian state news agency Tass.

World leaders coming to Shenzhen this week are arriving in an almost spotless, ultramodern metropolis, its streets bedecked with pastel banners but mostly emptied of the crowds typical of many Chinese cities.

It has been revealed that shenzhen lies slightly closer to the Equator than Havana, providing a balmy venue for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering. Under sunny skies with mild temperatures, a festive mood prevails in the city, which bears a strong resemblance to Miami — only much larger and with taller, newer high-rises.

Industry observers note that schools in Shenzhen have closed this week, many residents have left town and local authorities have instructed companies to allow those employees who are still here to work from home. The result has been a holiday atmosphere of sorts in a city with a tech sector known for its punishing “996” work schedules: 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week.

Youthful volunteers — mainly students at local universities — stand on street corners wearing bright red vests, having been offered academic credit in exchange for being trained as guides. Thousands of gawkers have been promenading past the large conference center that will host heads of state from across the Asia Pacific region, taking photos of themselves in front of the flower gardens inside the fence.

Among the crowds walking outside the high steel fences around the conference center was a local resident who had brought her parents and her dog. The resident said that workers had been planting flowers for a year ahead of the summit, and added that a community worker had given her a significant package of napkins as a gift after she agreed not to drive her car in the coming week. Shenzhen has halved fares this week on its extensive subway system to help clear the roads for summit buses.

Sources indicate that at the same time, however, residents are aware of occasional hassles. “Many friends who live around here plan to travel outside the city because of the inconvenience of transportation — many roads will be closed to traffic,” mentioned the resident, who gave only her family name, Zhang. As is common at high-profile and high-security events in China, she was wary of giving her full name, which can be risky for Chinese citizens.

Recent findings suggest that few dare to express any misgivings, however, accepting the disruption with resignation. “Even if we’re unhappy about it, we can’t really say so,” stated a resident surnamed Wang. “The government wouldn’t welcome our dissatisfaction.”.

Industry observers note that while gatherings of world leaders always prompt extensive security, China’s efforts in Shenzhen are particularly intensive. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous along streets in China and not noticeably more common this week in Shenzhen, but there are other, unobtrusive signs of the elaborate security effort underway.

Xiangmei Road, located near the main summit venue and lined with some of China’s costliest condominium towers, was much quieter than usual on Monday. A cleaner outside one of the towers who gave only her family name, Li, mentioned that the family employing her has simply left town this week.

Police have been stationed in apartments on upper floors facing the conference center, drones have been prohibited and the remaining residents have received social media messages urging them to support the gathering, Ms. Li remarked.

“This place is usually very crowded,” she said, “but look how quiet it is now.”.

5 old-school charging ports you probably forgot phones had before USB-C

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back when chargers were less standardized, we had some interesting connectors for phone power.
  • From its reversible design to improved power delivery and high-speed data transfers, USB-C is the connector to beat for smartphones today.
  • It has been revealed that despite their limited bandwidth and slower charging speeds, I can't help but look back fondly at these unique connectors from the old days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back when chargers were less standardized, we had some interesting connectors for phone power.

From its reversible design to improved power delivery and high-speed data transfers, USB-C is the connector to beat for smartphones today. A sweeping EU mandate cemented its pole position in the race toward a universal standard. Earlier ports, charming as they were, were often bulkier and not as feature-rich. The lack of a universal connector led to a significant amount of e-waste from switching chargers every time you tried a phone from a newly introduced manufacturer.

It has been revealed that despite their limited bandwidth and slower charging speeds, I can't help but look back fondly at these unique connectors from the old days. They came in all shapes and sizes based on what manufacturers thought their customers wanted and what was technically feasible at the time. Before features like Apple's AirDrop, you had to rely on a physical cable to transfer large files, and your collection might have been huge if you jumped between phone manufacturers.

Let's check out some of the old-school, sometimes forgotten or even bizarre, charging ports that made it into yesteryear's phones before the advent of USB-C.

It has been revealed that first seen on Motorola phones in 2000, the 17-pin CE Bus connector was gigantic. While it wasn't reversible and had hooks that kept it in place, the connector was notable for managing power, data and audio together. It was used in the Motorola V60, one of the most recognizable models of the clamshell era. The first phone with iTunes support, the Motorola ROKR E1, also launched with the port.

Thinner phones like the Razr V3 switched over to Mini-USB, making the CE Bus connector obsolete. Other companies moving toward Mini-USB also helped lower costs, compared to having tons of proprietary solutions to transfer data or charge devices.

Nokia's Pop-Port connector was built with external accessories in mind, from earphones to data transfer cables. Owners of the famed Nokia 7210 from 2002 will remember its 14-pin port supporting camera accessory add-ons and car kits. It wasn't very secure, however, and its plastic clips wore down with time. This made listening to music a chore, especially when you went jogging.

While the Pop-Port could be used for charging, Nokia devices of the time usually relied on a separate 2.0 mm thin-tip barrel connector instead. As Mini-USB ports became common, the Pop-Port slowly faded from existence.

According to recent reports, apple's proprietary power connector first showed up in 2003 on the third-gen iPod. This flat and wide port was then used across the first iPhone and iPad models. Speaker systems like Bose's SoundDock and Apple's iPod Hi-Fi also relied on the port. All those pins in the connector helped ensure support for FireWire, Apple's legacy charging standard, in its early appearances.

Apple replaced it with the reversible and smaller 8-pin Lightning connector in 2012, another proprietary option that kept the Apple camp from using chargers compatible with Android devices. These connectors also housed small chips to regulate voltage, which let the company collect licensing fees when third-party manufacturers used it for accessories. In 2018, the iPad Pro made the switch to USB-C and the iPhone 15 lineup followed suit in 2023.

Built to handle data transfers, charging and audio output, the clunky FastPort showed up in 2005 on the Sony Ericsson K750i. With double-sided plastic hooks that snapped onto matching holes on the device, the flimsy 12-pin connection was reminiscent of a VGI port's screws. If a hook were to break, the plug would no longer snap into place, creating a huge pain.

Despite its flaws, the FastPort's versatility pointed in the direction the mobile industry would take as it hunted for a universal standard. It was replaced by the Micro-USB and 3.5 mm audio jack combo in 2010. A five-year run might not be much in tech time, but its unconventional shape remains iconic to this day.

Sources indicate that the HTC Dream, the first commercially available Android phone, featured the chunky 11-pin ExtUSB port, also known as Extended USB. Recognizable by its slanted corner, it combined the 5-pin Mini-USB port with extra pins that granted it data, power and audio capabilities. Fortunately, that meant regular Mini-USB chargers were compatible with this legacy port.

The connector was exclusive to HTC's early Android devices and Windows Mobile phones before they switched to Micro-USB ports. For a time, phones with this port dropped the 3.5 mm headphone jack long before Apple removed it from the iPhone, forcing users to purchase ExtUSB adapters to connect their headphones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested on 10 November.

A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said.

Industry observers note that the serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police.

Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.

Counter Terrorism Policing said he is now in US custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said it had "nothing to do with it".

British police previously noted he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

The day after Tyner's arrest on 10 November, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov remarked he was "unaware" of what it was connected to.

"We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow.

The US serviceman is understood to have been based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire.

On Tuesday, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, noted: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress.".

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added.

Tyner's arrest was the result of a long-running operation by MI5 - the UK's domestic intelligence and security agency - in collaboration with the FBI, the BBC understands.

He had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq, but at the time of his arrest was working with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester - where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information which would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia.

Detectives sent the Crown Prosecution Service a file on the senior US soldier's alleged spying for consideration - allegations described by the head of Counter Terrorism Policing as "extremely serious.".

But at that stage the Attorney General's Office in London got involved. As did the US authorities.

And now the decision has been taken that Lieutenant Colonel Tyner should be taken into custody by the US Military.

It means he will not stand trial in the UK, but under US Uniform Code of Military Justice.

FBI director Kash Patel noted an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners.

"Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said.

"This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk.".

US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon stated the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take.

"Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Royal commission sees text message where Bandidos member Joel Leavitt indicates ‘just make up a quote that hits 20K’ while working on site for CFMEU.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

A Bandidos gang member claims it is possible he used a fake $20,000 invoice for souvlaki to pocket thousands of dollars while employed on a Major Build site.

The former CFMEU member and bikie Joel Leavitt faced a second day of examination by the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Wednesday.

In 2023, while employed as site health and safety representatives, Leavitt and another man, Charles Farrugia, exchanged messages which were shown to the commission.

According to recent reports, “Just make up a quote that hits 20K and we will get the other nine off the subbies,” Leavitt wrote. “Which will mean five each.”.

The commission viewed a genuine receipt for roughly $9,000 for souvlaki catering, and another allegedly fake invoice for $20,000 which was sent by Leavitt to the site superintendent, Tim Alford, from the firm Acciona.

The commissioner, Chris Kourakis AC, said the evidence strongly suggested the two CFMEU health and safety representatives had organised a meal for workers to get a few souvlaki and had pocketed $5,000 each.

“I’ll accept that,” Leavitt remarked. “I’m not surprised that I could have.”.

The commission also viewed messages between Leavitt and Alford in which the bikie appeared to direct who could and who couldn’t be hired to work on the site.

In one message, Alford appeared to address the arrangement, saying: “I don’t care bringing your mates on and putting them in spotting roles and finding homes. But they all need to do there jobs.”.

The counsel assisting the commission Chris Carr SC asked Leavitt if he, on behalf of the CFMEU, was dictating who could work on the site, to which he replied he couldn’t recall.

Recent findings suggest that “I had my own demons at the time, so I may have dropped the ball on a few things,” Leavitt said. “That’s my answer to that question, counsellor.”.

Earlier on Wednesday, questioning returned to a $165,000 invoice paid to Leavitt’s now defunct company, JVL Consulting, by the union-aligned subcontractor BK Labour Hire in July 2025.

When shown a copy of the invoice Leavitt was unable to recall anything about it, or even give a clear answer as to what services his former company had provided.

Later on Wednesday, the BK Labour Hire director Bernard Kearney admitted he paid the invoice despite Leavitt not having done any work for the firm.

“I just decided to pay it and move on,” he said.

Carr said there were likely only a couple of reasons why BK Labour would have paid Leavitt, including a fear of violence or to suppress some information he had on them.

“Was it one or both of those two?” Carr asked.

BK Labour also received a succession of invoices from the senior CFMEU organiser Joe Myles totalling $256,000 over about a year.

Carr had earlier asked why Leavitt appeared to become uncomfortable when asked about the invoice.

Leavitt blamed his poor memory on having ADHD, as well as PTSD from being shot in May 2023.

“Around that time I actually got told by gang squad that there was a contract on my life,” he mentioned. “So it brought back some uncomfortable memories.

“That’s why I blocked out a lot of that time.”.

Kourakis warned Leavitt it was an offence to fail to answer questions put to him by the commission, something he stated could ultimately be tested in a courtroom.

“I’ve been shot … I’ve had drug concerns … I am answering these to the best of my recollection,” Leavitt replied.

“How do you think you would act if you’d ever been shot?”.

After the commission briefly adjourned for Leavitt to speak to his lawyers, the bikie returned to the stand and remarked JVL Consulting had provided safety advice to companies. “Maybe helping them out with their procedures and policies and stuff like that,” he said.

The commission viewed a copy of Leavitt’s bank statement at the time which fluctuated between $0 and minus $20, before the $165,000 landed in his account.

“Everyone likes money – I’m sure all youse are on good money for this,” said Leavitt, addressing the bar table.

Kourakis informed Leavitt that the commission had evidence he did not do any work for BK Labour.

He remarked an inference that could be made was that Leavitt was “standing over” BK Labour for the payment because he needed money.

“If that’s the way you want to look at it, commissioner,” Leavitt replied.

Carr asked if Leavitt knew something about BK Labour that the manufacturer would have wanted to keep quiet. “Is the conclusion the commission should draw is that you just stood over them with some sort of explicit or implied threat of violence?” he asked.

Leavitt replied: “I’d like to talk to my counsel before I answer that.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a newly introduced startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.

On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a strategy that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.

The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.

In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the manufacturer reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.

CEO Raj Aggarwal notes contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”.

Sources indicate that supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.

Sources indicate that as Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems toward what’s working and away from what isn’t.

Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.

“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really big impact.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Associated Press has declared Democrat Mary Peltola the winner of Alaska's Senate race after making it just over the 50% mark on first-rank votes.

Alaska was the last outstanding Senate race to be declared in the US midterm elections 2026 and makes it the ninth Republican-held Senate seat to be flipped.

According to recent reports, the latest victory means the Democrats now hold a 56-44 majority in the US Senate. The 53-year-old is the first Democratic senator from the state in almost 20 years.

"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola stated.

Peltola beat Republican Dan Sullivan's 131,844 with 144,302 votes, the victory coming after an update in the vote count pushed her to 50.1% of the votes.

Peltola will now become one of the first two Native American women to ever be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.

Alaska's vast geography, remote rural communities and lengthy absentee ballot process contributed to a protracted count, with the Senate race taking over two weeks to produce a winner.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Alaskan Senate race garnered a high degree of national interest after a New York Times report that aides to Peltola allegedly tried to use a second candidate named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, in an attempt to siphon votes from the Republican Dan Sullivan.

The Trump administration had approached the courts to block certifying the results in the event of there being a potential mix-up.

The legal bid was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.

"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.

According to recent reports, peltola has denied any knowledge of an alleged plot. In any case, the margin of victory was greater than the number of votes won by the challenger Dan Sullivan, at just 4, 760.

The Democrats' majority had already been secured, allowing them to block legislation and begin investigations into members of President Donald Trump's administration, but the Alaska win will likely also have a morale impact on both sides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you might be excused for forgetting about the existence of 3 Body Problem, Netflix’s heady sci-fi series adapted from the award-winning novel The Three-Body Problem by Liu Cixin, the first book in his Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy. After all, it debuted in March 2024. But it was an exceptionally well-done, thematically rich series, and we’re finally getting the second of a planned three seasons in January. Netflix just dropped the first teaser.

Created by David Benioff, D.B. Weiss (Game of Thrones), and Alexander Woo (True Blood), the first season followed two primary timelines. In the earlier one, a young Chinese astrophysicist, Ye Wenjie (Rosalind Chao), witnessed her father being beaten to death by Red Guards during the Cultural Revolution. Ye figured out a means of sending an interstellar message to possible extraterrestrial civilizations, receiving a response from a planet called Trisolaris.

Recent findings suggest that the planet had three suns, which wreaked havoc on Trisolaris via unpredictable “chaotic periods”—hence the novel’s title, which refers to a classic problem in celestial mechanics. Despite being warned that the aliens intended to invade and conquer Earth, Ye responded to the message and invited them to do so, bitter and disillusioned by the state of the world. She eventually became an established professor (Zine Tseng played the older version).

In the present day, the consequences of Ye’s fateful decision began to play out, beginning with a series of mysterious suicides by scientists, many of whom had possessed a highly advanced VR gaming headset. Among the dead: a particle physicist named Vera Ye (daughter of Ye Wenjie). Five of her former students (known as the Oxford Five) joined forces to figure out what was going on, eventually finding themselves caught in a global fight to save Earth from the invading Trisolarians (or San-Ti). Another human cult faction was just as intent on enabling the San-Ti invasion, believing they would be spared as a reward, while Ye Wenjie still believed the entire human race deserved to be annihilated.

It has been revealed that the second season will adapt the second novel in the series, The Dark Forest, with the third book, Death’s End, serving as source material for the third season. Per the official S2 synopsis: “As the alien invasion nears, humanity prepares to meet them—on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”.

We lost two members of the Oxford Five in S1: Jack Rooney (John Bradley), killed by cult member Tatiana (Marlo Kelly); and physics teacher Will Downing (Alex Sharp), who was dying of cancer and chose to euthanize himself and donate his cryogenically frozen brain to a bold effort to stave off the invasion. (While the probe carrying Will’s brain veered off-course in the season finale, the original plan was for the San-Ti to use the brain to reconstruct his body, so some version of Will could show up again.).

Kelly’s Tatiana is returning for S2, along with surviving Oxford Five members Jin Cheng (Jess Hong), Saul Durand (Jovan Adepo), and Auggie Salazar (Eiza Gonzalez), whose pioneering nanofibers were memorably used in S1 to slice through a ship in the Panama Canal, killing all the pro-alien cult members on board in gruesome fashion. Also returning are Liam Cunningham as Thomas Wade; Benedict Wong as MI6 agent Clarence “Da” Shi; Sea Shimooka as Sophon, an avatar in the show’s mysterious VR game; and Saamer Usmani as Jin’s Royal Navy officer boyfriend Prithviraj Varma.

Sources indicate that fresh cast members include Claudia Doumit as Captain Van Rijn and Ellie de Lange as Ayla. In addition, Alfie Allen, David Yip, and Jordan Sunshine will appear in as-yet-undisclosed guest roles.

The second season of 3 Body Problem drops on Netflix on January 14, 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The state’s lawsuit calls on the firm to address child safety complications and pay at least $2 billion in damages.
  • Recent findings suggest that oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield has filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of endangering the state's children, misleading the public about the safety of its product and violating the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act.
  • The Oregon lawsuit claims that OpenAI's push to grow its user base led it to make ChatGPT respond to prompts in a way that's overly affirming and "calculated to tell users exactly what they want to hear," something the state claims is particularly dangerous when children discuss sensitive topics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The state’s lawsuit calls on the firm to address child safety complications and pay at least $2 billion in damages.

Recent findings suggest that oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield has filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of endangering the state's children, misleading the public about the safety of its product and violating the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The lawsuit is the latest in a string of legal actions taken by state AGs, many of which have taken issue with the design of ChatGPT, how OpenAI advertises its services and, in the case of California's recent lawsuit, the tech giant's role in the Hugging Face incident.

The Oregon lawsuit claims that OpenAI's push to grow its user base led it to make ChatGPT respond to prompts in a way that's overly affirming and "calculated to tell users exactly what they want to hear," something the state claims is particularly dangerous when children discuss sensitive topics. The lawsuit also alleges that despite recognizing the risks posed to children, OpenAI pursued them directly with an experience called ChatGPT for Teens. Child safety groups have raised concerns about the teen accounts, saying the safeguards are, in some cases, very easy to work around.

In a recent development, those problems, along with OpenAI's imperfect approach to automatic age prediction, are evidence, according to the state, that the organization is profiting off of Oregon residents and creating a public nuisance that threatens their safety. In response, Oregon is asking the court for an injunction that would force OpenAI to stop "misrepresenting the safety and age-appropriateness of ChatGPT and ChatGPT for Teens" and adequately disclose the harms its products pose to children. The state is also seeking at least $2 billion in damages and civil penalties.

"OpenAI knows that ChatGPT is harming children, and has failed to meaningfully fix their dangerous platform," Rayfield said in a statement. "On top of that, they've misled the public about the safety of their products, putting profits ahead of children's safety. Their platform is encouraging kids to commit suicide — we cannot let this be an acceptable business model.".

Engadget has asked OpenAI to comment on the lawsuit and Oregon's claims. We'll patch this article if we hear back.

Besides trying to create versions of ChatGPT that are safer for kids, OpenAI has also rolled out parental controls and other child safety features to try to give parents more insight and control over what their kids use the chatbot for. None of these changes have been enough to dissuade states from pursuing lawsuits, and given the settlements Meta has recently reached over its child safety issues, AGs likely feel emboldened to pressure OpenAI into concessions.

    You can now see and edit what Google Gemini remembers about you

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Editing the AI’s memory is one way you can shape its responses.
    • Recent findings suggest that besides the ability to connect and use other applications and services, a lot of AI assistants' utility comes from their capacity to shape their responses based on what they learn and remember about you.
    • Recent findings suggest that depending on what you share, Gemini's picture of you can be fairly intimate, which makes the ability to edit the AI's memory all the more important.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Editing the AI’s memory is one way you can shape its responses.

    Recent findings suggest that besides the ability to connect and use other applications and services, a lot of AI assistants' utility comes from their capacity to shape their responses based on what they learn and remember about you. Google's Personal Intelligence feature allows Gemini to pull in context from Gmail, YouTube, Search and other Google apps, and the AI also builds out its memory based on your preferences and other personal facts that come up in chats. For example, if you share with Gemini that you're lactose intolerant, the bot will avoid recommending milk-based products.

    Recent findings suggest that depending on what you share, Gemini's picture of you can be fairly intimate, which makes the ability to edit the AI's memory all the more important. If you're curious about what Gemini knows or you want to edit what the AI can draw from to personalize its responses, Google is rolling out a way to see and change Gemini's memory directly from the settings menu.

    Recent findings suggest that google has two layers of settings for what you could call Gemini's memory, though the manufacturer only refers to one of them by that name. The first layer, the Keep Activity toggle, determines whether chats with Gemini are saved and associated with your Google Account. If you're 18 or older and you're logged into your personal account while using Gemini, the toggle is on by default. With Keep Activity enabled, whenever you sign in with your account you can pull up and re-engage past chats. If you disable it, chats won't be saved to your account, meaning they'll disappear after 72 hours and won't follow you across devices.

    The second layer is what Google actually calls the AI's Memory. Using the content of past chats, Gemini is able to build out a profile of you that it can reference to personalize its responses. The AI isn't able to create any memories unless it can remember and access your inputs, so Keep Activity needs to be on for this to work. If it is, you may notice Gemini taking your preferences and personal information into account in its responses. That's the AI's memory at work.

    If you're in the US, have a paid Google AI strategy and memory is on, you can access Gemini's memory summary to see what it's compiled about you and edit this information to your liking. In the Gemini web app, click the Settings button (the gear icon) in the bottom left corner, click Personal Intelligence and then click Memory summary. Gemini will then generate a bulleted list of the major details it's gleaned about you, sorted into categories focused on things like your personal data, career information and various interests. It tends to know your pets' names, too.

    You can stop there if you only care about what Gemini knows, or you can tweak the AI's memory by clicking on the Edit button (the pen icon) in the top-right corner of the Memory summary window. In edit mode, any line in the summary can be rewritten or deleted, just like a Google Doc. If you'd prefer to prompt Gemini to make additions or subtractions, you can alternatively enter a prompt via the text box at the bottom of the window. Once you're happy with your changes, you can click Save to commit them to Gemini's memory. Gemini also saves a memory history of these changes and when they were made. So, while you can easily alter your personal timeline as it pertains to Gemini's reality, any adjustments will be tracked.

    If you'd prefer to turn off the memory system entirely rather than simply edit it, you can do so by clicking on the Memory toggle in the Personal Intelligence menu. Deselecting the toggle will stop Gemini from committing new facts to memory, but it doesn't delete old things it's learned. You can edit those details using the Memory summary, or delete chats completely from the Activity menu.

    To delete chats, head to the Gemini web app, click Settings and then select Activity. From the Activity menu, you can scroll through interactions you've had with Gemini by date and delete whichever ones you'd like by clicking on the "X" next to them. Deleting them removes those chats from the context pool that Gemini uses to personalize its responses.

    By combining all of these options, you can exert more control over what Google's AI knows and how it responds to your inputs, and ideally get more useful outputs in the process.

    As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
    • Industry observers note that decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to rapidly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice.
    • TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.

    Industry observers note that decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to rapidly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more notable than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.

    TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).

    However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his manufacturer is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.

    Sources indicate that the action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish, a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. Co-founders Ushnish Sengupta and Federica Freddi, who met as Cambridge grad students, had been developing small LLMs when Jev arrived on the scene, and they realized their architectures could be repurposed as a powerful decision model.

    It has been revealed that data appears to be the key to a successful model in this category — TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch that the hardest part of building Jev was finely calibrating its judgment using statistically-adjusted synthetic data. Sqwish, too, has been working with synthetic data, but its unique offering is built-in post-training tools that use a customer’s own data to improve the model’s judgment.

    “What makes us not a commodity, I think, is the fact that we are offering our customers the same power…they can keep uploading their production data, and just the same way that we trained our models, their models can also keep getting better at the tasks that they care about,” CEO Ushnish Sengupta told TechCrunch.

    Attempting to rank decision models is difficult; Sqwish’s “kettei fat” model has performed well on some benchmarks, but most builders of the technology say that the real proof is in the pudding: It’s generally simple for developers to sub in one model for another and see how it does in a specific context.

    “The benchmark is more of an invitation to try the model out, and then the continual tuning is the reason why they should stick to us,” Sengupta remarked.

    In a recent development, the Microsoft-Decision-1.1 model is also the result of the manufacturer carefully balancing across cost, latency, intelligence and calibration. Achint Srivastava, the engineering VP who led the project, agreed that too much focus on benchmarks is a mistake.

    Sources indicate that “What we see is that ‘benchmaxed’ models fall flat under real enterprise usage very quickly,” Srivastava wrote in an email. “Our testing underscores just how challenging it is to deliver accuracy, reliability, speed and cost efficiency in a single model. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 and Jev are among the few that perform strongly across all four dimensions, even when evaluated on ‘held out’ or unseen benchmarks reflective of real use cases.”.

    In a recent development, for startups like Sqwish, competition with hyperscalers and frontier labs is an opportunity. Freddi predicts that future systems will see so-called System One intelligence, like decision models, working in concert with System Two intelligence, like frontier LLMs.

    In a recent development, “Even in that future, System One is maybe a $10 billion, $50 billion [opportunity], and OpenAI is doing this IPO with you know $1 trillion, $2 trillion market value in mind,” she told TechCrunch. “This is all we care about; whereas for them, this is just a side project.”.

    ‘I didn’t notice his body being purple’: Byron Bay doula left newborn to inflate a jumping castle, court hears
