    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Inquest into deaths of four babies born in free births or at home in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 hears ‘something was seriously wrong’.
    • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • Baby DH was born in an inflatable pool, in a candle-lit room in his parents’ home near Byron Bay, with no one medically trained present.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Inquest into deaths of four babies born in free births or at home in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 hears ‘something was seriously wrong’.

    Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

    Baby DH was born in an inflatable pool, in a candle-lit room in his parents’ home near Byron Bay, with no one medically trained present. There are two very different versions of what happened next.

    In a recent development, in the parents’ version, the doula reassured them Baby DH was OK, then left to inflate a jumping castle while their newborn turned purple, became floppy, and struggled to breathe. In the doula’s version, everything seemed OK but she suggested they seek more help if they wanted to.

    The Upcoming South Wales coroner’s court heard the two competing narratives on Wednesday as part of an ongoing inquest into the deaths of four babies born in free births or home births.

    The babies died in NSW’s northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024.

    Baby DH lived for just over eight hours.

    “The evidence will be that from his first minutes of life, [Baby DH] showed signs that something was seriously wrong,” the Lismore courtroom heard.

    It has been revealed that “His parents saw those signs. They raised them again and again with their doula, who they had engaged to watch for exactly that. Their doula, in this case, was a woman named Amy Lou Smith.

    Industry observers note that “Each time the parents raised their concerns, they were reassured by Amy Lou. An ambulance was not called until moments before [Baby DH] stopped breathing.”.

    Recent findings suggest that his father described the baby as floppy after birth. “His colour, his whole body was purple with his hands and feet darker still,” the court heard, and Smith told them some purple in the hands and feet was normal.

    “I didn’t notice his body being purple,” Smith told the court.

    According to recent reports, told the baby’s colour wasn’t improving, Smith said “as long as his abdomen isn’t purple”, according to evidence from the parents. The mother was shocked. His whole body had been purple all along. His temperature was low, 34.5C. Smith suggested trying to get it up to 37C.

    “I believed if they had real concerns, that they would call an ambulance and not be texting a non medically trained doula,” Smith told the court.

    Smith, the inquest heard, described his laboured breathing as “cute little noises”. “I didn’t say that,” Smith told the court.

    The court heard Smith told the couple Baby DH would have been put on oxygen if he was in hospital. But Smith later told the court she didn’t know what the hospital would have done.

    Industry observers note that he had strange lumps on his body, and wasn’t feeding. Smith suggested they get the lumps checked out, and warned that babies sometimes take a while to latch on to the breast, according to the parents’ evidence.

    The court heard Smith left to set up a jumping castle for her son’s birthday. She sent the couple a picture of the castle later, as they were trying to contact a doctor, the court heard.

    Smith told the court the castle was already set up, and the couple was happy for her to leave.

    “Everything felt like it was OK,” she noted.

    It has been revealed that eventually, the parents spoke to the GP they had tried to contact earlier. The GP told them to call triple zero. They did, and did CPR until the paramedics got there. But Baby DH was declared dead at the hospital.

    After the father had made the emergency call, Smith also told them to call an ambulance, and sent them instructions on infant CPR.

    Throughout the hearing, Smith denied that any of her advice or comments constituted clinical advice.

    Neonatologist Dr Paul Evans, the court heard, had found Baby DH had a complex heart defect, one that would have shown up on an X-ray. The baby could have been treated, and a birth plan with proximity to a major hospital and specialist cardiac care prepared, the court heard.

    The child’s death was not inevitable, Evans found.

    Industry observers note that while pregnant, Baby DH’s mother decided to rely on a doula. She first approached a woman the court heard was likely to be Sita Tara Kali, a self-described birth keeper who was also involved in the care of another baby previously mentioned during the inquest. But Kali didn’t feel she could help, so they turned to Smith.

    In a recent development, the court heard the couple paid for an online “sovereign birth course” for Smith and was reassured that she had enough experience. They agreed on an emergency blueprint.

    Smith, who became a birth doula in 2020, was quizzed on her experience in court.

    She has a degree in fine art and has worked as a social worker and a youth worker.

    Industry observers note that she told the court she is not medically trained in any way but did an online “full-spectrum doula course”. She learned CPR but was not familiar with how to apply it to a newborn – she denied she had given the parents the impression she was.

    She had no training about a newborn’s colour, breathing, or feeding, but she did go to a retreat where she learned about referring a woman to more support if needed.

    Recent findings suggest that she had been present at 15 births over four years, nine alongside a midwife, and conceded she didn’t know what a low-risk birth would look like. She had read a couple of books about birthing, but they were more “spiritual”, the court heard.

    She agreed that she now believes the best model of care for a home birth is for a clinically trained midwife to work alongside a doula.

    Breaking: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean.
    • After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.
    • The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean.

    After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.

    The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.

    Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, unveiled that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".

    The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.

    The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.

    Industry observers note that the measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to fresh infections.

    The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.

    PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.

    "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination.".

    He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission.

    Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, noted that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates.

    US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years.

    Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections.

    Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status".

    "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency mentioned.

    CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans.

    In a recent development, "Vaccination does," she noted. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities.".

    In a post on social media, Kennedy stated: "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.".

    Recent findings suggest that "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also stated. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment.".

    The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

    Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, remarked the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards".

    The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

    Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths.

    But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana noted patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems.

    The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns.

    The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity - which limits the spread of measles.

    An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials.

    Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database.

    Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics.

    The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge.

    President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine.

    Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana remarked. "We need a clear message from the top.".

    The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that firaxis Games, the studio behind the Civilization and XCOM franchises of computer strategy games, last week laid off about a third of its staff, totaling around 60 people. That’s according to a recent report in Bloomberg.

    The report cites people “familiar with the cuts,” saying that the flagship game the studio is currently working on, a newly introduced entry in the XCOM series, “has faced development struggles and missed a significant milestone.” The departures also include the studio head, Heather Hazen.

    A Firaxis spokesperson released the following statement:.

    Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.

    Sources indicate that the storied studio has had a rough run of things of late. Its most recent game, Civilization VII, launched to solid enough sales but divided players in terms of reception. Players have long criticized new Civilization titles for being barebones compared to immediate predecessors that have seen multiple post-launch updates and expansions, but the response was sharper this time.

    The game has found more fans in recent months, but a portion of the Civilization audience will likely never fully warm to it due to its ages system—a design choice that partially solved many long-standing pacing problems, but at the cost of altering the core experience.

    Recent findings suggest that before that, Firaxis worked on Marvel’s Midnight Suns, which had a more positive reception in terms of sentiment but does not seem to have sold as many units as the company had hoped. Now, with the new XCOM title facing challenges, that’s three troubled games in a row.

    In a recent development, to top it off, most of Firaxis’ direct competitors in the strategy game market are much leaner and not beholden to a major publisher. (The publisher for the Civilization franchise is 2K Games, which lives under the same tech giant that publishes the soon-to-launch Grand Theft Auto VI.).

    Industry observers note that the industry at large has seen widespread layoffs and studio closures over the past few years. There’s no single reason for that; rather, there are numerous factors, including contraction after COVID-era over-investment, increased competition, changes in leadership culture at major publishers, and larger economic factors beyond the scope of just the games industry.

    #23824. How to set up EV routing on CarPlay and Android Auto

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (936 w)

    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    How to set up EV routing on CarPlay and Android Auto

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Whether EV routing works depends on your car, your phone and the navigation app you use.
    • Recent findings suggest that owning an electric car means you need to adapt your driving to your surroundings.
    • You could find charging stations yourself and add them as stops on your trip, but that's not ideal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Whether EV routing works depends on your car, your phone and the navigation app you use.

    Recent findings suggest that owning an electric car means you need to adapt your driving to your surroundings. You're not worrying about where to fill up your gas tank anymore, but about where to find the nearest charging station. Long trips mean you're likely to need to top off your EV's battery; otherwise you're going to reach an abrupt end.

    You could find charging stations yourself and add them as stops on your trip, but that's not ideal. EV routing can take some of the hassle out of planning. It'll plan stops around your route with an idea of when you're arriving and how much charge you'll have left. Google Maps and Apple Maps both feature EV routing on CarPlay and Android Auto, but there are some differences, and it isn't universal. You'll need to know what your car supports and how to use your navigation app.

    Before you grab your keys, check that your car supports the EV routing features you need. Just having CarPlay or Android Auto doesn't guarantee support, unfortunately. Some cars will also work directly with EV features through CarPlay, while others might need an extra app to link the car to Apple Maps.

    Sources indicate that ford's Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning support Apple Maps EV routing, as do Toyota's 2023 and newer EVs in the US. Google expanded Android Auto's charging recommendations to more than 350 US EV models in March 2026.

    Sources indicate that android Auto isn't the same as having Google Maps built into your car. Android Auto displays the apps from your phone, but if your car already has Google Maps built in, it'll run directly on your infotainment system with access to the car's battery data.

    There are three ways for EV routing to work on Apple Maps via CarPlay. For cars that don't need a manufacturer app installed, connect your iPhone to CarPlay while you're parked, then open the Apple Maps app. Search for your final destination to get your directions, then tap Connect above the list of available routes.

    In a recent development, if your car needs a manufacturer app installed, you'll need to download it from the App Store first. Once it's installed and set up, open Apple Maps, tap your profile picture then tap Vehicles > Connect Your Electric Vehicles. Follow any of the on-screen instructions to complete the process. You'll be able to set up your preferred charging network at this point, too.

    Some manufacturers have their own connection process in their app. Toyota owners, for example, tap Find > Apple Maps EV Routing, agree to the terms, then tap Connect Vehicle to Apple Maps and follow any extra instructions. Once connected, you'll be able to track your EV's battery levels in the app, with appropriate charging stops recommended on your route and live charger availability in some cases. When your battery drops too low, Maps will route you to the nearest compatible charger.

    Check your network preferences, too. Ford suggests Tesla Superchargers as the preferred network for some Mustang owners, and Apple Maps can prioritize them, though you'll need the right fast-charging adapter.

    Make sure Google Maps is up to date on your phone. Google says you'll need version 25.44 or later for battery estimates to work.

    Next, head to Google Maps and tap your profile icon, then tap Settings > Your vehicles. Select Electric as your engine type, then tap Add vehicle. You'll be asked to choose the make, model, year and trim. Double-check the connections listed under Your plugs and edit them if you need to, then tap Save to confirm.

    Recent findings suggest that at this point, connect to Android Auto and confirm your car details when prompted. Start planning your trip in Google Maps and you'll see the estimated battery usage and an Add charging button on your car's display. Select that, add your starting battery percentage and then confirm. Google Maps will then add charging stops to your trip and display your predicted arrival battery percentage. You can change these stops and set a preferred arrival battery level, too.

    In a recent development, don't take the prediction as gospel, though. Live driving conditions, your car's condition and the weather can all affect the estimate, so keep an eye on your charge level as you drive.

    It's easier to use Google Maps or Apple Maps for EV routing, but there are other options. For instance, the A Better Routeplanner app (or ABRP for short) supports EV-specific trip planning. You can add your car model and a destination, and it'll generate routes with charging stops on the way. You can use it on your dashboard through CarPlay or Android Auto if you've got an ABRP Premium subscription.

    ABRP does support live battery information in some cars if you're running Android Auto, but you'll need to give it the Car information permission in the app's settings. There's no equivalent option for CarPlay consumers, though.

    Recent findings suggest that you don't necessarily need EV routing to find compatible chargers. With your car profile set up, search Google Maps for charging stations and select Your plugs as the EV plug filter. You'll need to judge whether you can reach each stop on your current charge.

    Until EV charging stops are as ubiquitous as gas stations, you'll need to think a little more about where you can charge on long trips. Just make sure you leave plenty of charge between stops so you're not left running low with no chargers nearby.

    ‘Phantom forests’ in Australia’s arid outback used to create carbon credits meant to offset emissions, report claims

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Carbon credit companies reject research that found only small increase in forest and canopy cover in regeneration areas despite wet conditions.
    • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • A fight over the legitimacy of Australia’s climate change policy has reignited after researchers claimed “phantom forests” in the semi-arid outback are being used to create offsets that allow fossil fuel companies to keep pumping out pollution.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Carbon credit companies reject research that found only small increase in forest and canopy cover in regeneration areas despite wet conditions.

    Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

    A fight over the legitimacy of Australia’s climate change policy has reignited after researchers claimed “phantom forests” in the semi-arid outback are being used to create offsets that allow fossil fuel companies to keep pumping out pollution.

    A group of academics, including professors from the Australian National University and the University of Upcoming South Wales, said they had examined 50 forest regeneration projects used to create carbon credits.

    Led by Prof Andrew Macintosh, the former federal government carbon credit scheme integrity chair and the director of ANU’s Centre for Environmental Markets, the researchers said they found only a small increase in forest and tree crown cover in the areas over the past five years despite wet conditions.

    They said the conclusions were consistent with their previous peer-reviewed studies that found Australia’s method for creating carbon credits from forest regeneration was doing little to nothing to help address the climate crisis.

    Recent findings suggest that the research was published in a report released on Wednesday by the Australian Conservation Foundation. Prof David Eldridge, one of the report’s authors and a former principal research scientist with the NSW environment department, remarked he was “gobsmacked” that “phantom forests” in outback areas north-west of the remote town of Bourke could earn carbon credits for forest regrowth.

    “Some of these areas have never grown forests; they will never grow forests,” he said.

    The findings were rejected by companies that manage what are known as human-induced regeneration projects in north-western NSW. “These are some of the most closely examined carbon projects in the country, and the evidence on the ground shows they are working,” a spokesperson for Green Collar, a business that manages carbon credit projects, noted.

    Each carbon credit is mentioned to represent one tonne of emissions that has been removed from, or prevented from being released to, the atmosphere.

    Their use is contentious, in part, because industrial-polluting companies that are required to cut emissions under a federal policy known as the safeguard mechanism are allowed to buy an unlimited number of credits to count as their own cuts while continuing to pollute.

    Scientists have warned limiting the climate crisis requires rapid direct cuts in emissions and that carbon credits – also known as offsets – should be used sparingly.

    The Australian Conservation Foundation noted it showed coal and gas companies should be banned from claiming offsets as their own emissions cuts.

    Adam Bandt, the foundation’s chief executive and a former Australian Greens leader, said the safeguard mechanism was meant to “cut climate pollution and protect us from big coal and gas threatening our lives and livelihoods, but it’s not working”.

    “Putting more climate pollution into the atmosphere now could push us past dangerous tipping points. It can’t be offset, and the science tells us to keep coal and gas in the ground,” he mentioned.

    Macintosh mentioned the evidence showed the projects were by and large not regenerating forest, but had created more than 60m carbon credits worth up to $2bn.

    The report stated the safeguard mechanism was being “materially undermined” by poor-quality credits. It said a “flood of cheap, low integrity” credits was making it cheaper in many cases for significant polluters to pay for offsets rather than make direct emissions cuts.

    There have been more than 430 human-induced regeneration projects in Australia since 2013, covering an area of 38m hectares – larger than Japan. The federal government is now reviewing the safeguard policy, as required under legislation.

    A spokesperson for the Clean Energy Regulator, which manages the scheme, mentioned it took allegations about the integrity or efficacy of carbon credit projects seriously, and had confidence in the forest regeneration method.

    It said projects were required to demonstrate every five years that canopy cover was increasing, and it had rejected non-complying areas that could have received 6.7m carbon credits.

    Green Collar said it stood “firmly behind the integrity of its human-induced regeneration projects” and expressed frustration that the report had not been publicly released or published in a peer-reviewed journal. It said the researchers had “judged these carbon projects with satellite pictures and a single field visit”.

    Industry observers note that “Carbon is stored in stems, branches, leaves, roots and dead timber. Satellite canopy products see leaves from above. They do not measure the wood and roots where most of that carbon sits,” its spokesperson said.

    Skye Glenday, the chief executive of Climate Friendly, another carbon credit project developer, mentioned the criticisms of the carbon credit projects were “at odds with the facts and the extensive independent scientific and regulatory scrutiny that is applied to all projects”.

    “Debate about the use of offsets is legitimate, but let’s have that debate on its merits rather than undermining the carbon drawdown Australia also needs,” she mentioned.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dating optimism might be in, and not just because of the recent "blue wave." In its latest D.A.T.E. Report (Data, Advice, Trends, and Expertise), called Dating While Dreaming Major, Hinge found some hope in daters. Gen Z singles are seeing possibility in their future partners and how they can lead to their ideal future selves.

    Sources indicate that seventy-six percent of Gen Z imagine the person they want to become alongside their ideal partner, according to Hinge's July 2026 survey of over 13,000 people around the world, including Gen Z and millennial daters. One in four members of Gen Z (25 percent) is more likely than millennials to believe their ideal partner will help them achieve their ideal life, while two out of three (67 percent) prefer a partner who makes them feel hopeful and inspired.

    Industry observers note that only seven percent of Gen Z believe they'll achieve their life goals on their own, signaling that young adults want to enter a power couple of sorts. Or, maybe, what Hinge has coined as "the possibility couple," or a relationship where being together makes you feel more hopeful about the future. The best hookup apps, reviewed by our experts AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections Tinder — top pick for fast hookups Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups Pure — best for anonymous hookups OkCupid — best app for inclusivity Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

    AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

    Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

    Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

    Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

    But with all this optimism comes the pressure to find the perfect partner...which doesn't exist. And this is compounded by ever-growing uncertainty. Costs are high and don't seem to be going down, while the AI industry threatens to eat all of our jobs.

    It has been revealed that "Nowadays, there's a sense that if you want a good future, you have to strategy for it carefully," Hinge's lead relationship scientist, Logan Ury, stated in the report. "And that includes who you choose as a partner.".

    This desire for a perfect match — for your present and future — is showing up in how Gen Z is dating, too. Nearly 60 percent of Gen Z noted dating outside their ideal feels risky, and 44 percent said that straying away from it would feel like lowering their standards.

    This pressure for perfection is literally twofold for Gen Z women, who are nearly twice as likely as Gen Z men to say that knowing what they're looking for in a romantic connection helps them feel in control.

    Hinge's love and connection expert, Moe Ari Brown, advised in the report that having a checklist for a future partner isn't always the best way to find a real connection. Knowing what you want is different from deciding the exacts in advance. "Leaving room for the person in front of you can reveal possibilities a checklist can't," he noted.

    The good news is that Gen Z are 25 percent less likely than millennials to say that attraction develops immediately — leaving room for that possibility.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.
    • The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.

    The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.

    It has been revealed that openAI, by comparison, states it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.

    Sources indicate that google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that states chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.

    It has been revealed that the longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Consumers will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.

    Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for owners who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

    Business Council of Australia more aligned with fossil fuel industry than its members’ values, analysis finds

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Research by InfluenceMap raises questions about association’s policies and representation, particularly around advocacy for new gas supplies.
    • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • The Business Council of Australia is lobbying for gas expansion policies that clash with the climate concerns of the majority of its own members, according to latest research that raises questions about the sway of a handful of major companies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Research by InfluenceMap raises questions about association’s policies and representation, particularly around advocacy for new gas supplies.

    Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

    The Business Council of Australia is lobbying for gas expansion policies that clash with the climate concerns of the majority of its own members, according to latest research that raises questions about the sway of a handful of major companies.

    The business association also does not publicly disclose who is on its energy and climate committee, prompting transparency concerns among researchers over how its policies are shaped and whose interests they represent.

    Analysis by London-headquartered InfluenceMap found the BCA’s positions aligned more closely with energy companies Woodside, Santos and ConocoPhillips than with the majority of its corporate base, particularly on the energy transition where it has advocated for upcoming gas supplies over phasing down.

    InfluenceMap’s Australia lead, Jack Herring, said major associations such as the BCA are an influential voice in government policymaking.

    “These findings suggest the BCA’s climate policy engagement better reflects the narrow interests of members connected to the fossil fuel value chain than its wider membership,” Herring said.

    “Advocacy for fossil gas expansion risks undermining Australia’s climate targets and also threatens to create increased health risks and energy affordability and security concerns for everyday households, so this is an concern that affects us all.”.

    InfluenceMap’s analysis of organization positions shows more than two-thirds of the members assessed, including Qantas, Woolworths, Coles, Atlassian, Fortescue and major banks CBA and NAB, advocate for stronger climate policies than the business council itself.

    That support typically includes backing faster renewable energy rollout and advocating for more ambitious emission reduction targets.

    For the study, the thinktank assessed 58 companies – a representative sample of the BCA’s more than 120 members – drawing on thousands of public statements, government submissions and regulatory filings.

    Of those members assessed, 69% backed stronger climate policies than the BCA, a gap that widened to 78% on energy transition challenges.

    Herring said the BCA does not disclose who sits on its internal climate and energy committees, obscuring how its policy positions are formed.

    “We obviously do know who’s on the association board, but beyond that, there’s no transparency around those internal committees,” he remarked.

    A spokesperson for the BCA said the association supported the “national goal of achieving net zero by 2050 and the setting of interim targets, while also delivering reliable and affordable energy and ensuring we don’t undermine our international competitiveness along the way”.

    “The BCA has long advocated for gas as an essential part of the net zero transition – ensuring grid stability – while we move to greater reliance on renewable energy,” the spokesperson noted.

    The BCA declined to comment on the makeup of its climate and energy committee.

    The analysis comes as industry groups ramp up lobbying over the “safeguard mechanism”, Australia’s main policy for curbing emissions from its largest industrial facilities, which is under federal review.

    While the BCA and most significant resources companies publicly support the Paris agreement and Australia’s net zero 2050 carbon emissions target, they interpret what those commitments require in radically different ways to what is widely regarded as climate best practice.

    Several oil and gas producer members, including Woodside, argue that increased gas supply is required to support the shift to renewables and enhance energy security in language that has been adopted by the BCA.

    This rubs against those BCA members aligned with the findings of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, which found greenhouse gas emissions from existing fossil fuel infrastructure were more than enough to push the world beyond its climate goals.

    InfluenceMap also found that the business council frequently lobbies for a “technology-neutral” or “technology agnostic” energy transition, which is the same language used by the fossil fuel sector designed to steer renewable energy funding toward gas.

    Persephone Fraser, the ethical research and climate policy lead at fund manager Australian Ethical, mentioned misaligned lobbying was a significant risk for companies and their shareholders, and a major risk to the economy.

    “Companies must be scrutinising what is being advocated for in their name and actively correcting the record when it is inconsistent with their own positions, and interests,” Fraser said.

    “Membership of an industry association cannot mean outsourcing responsibility for climate lobbying.”.

    #23816. Tech Report: Here's what you can do if your PC won't read an external hard drive

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (776 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Here's what you can do if your PC won't read an external hard drive

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bring a dead external drive back to life with these troubleshooting steps, including Disk Utility and swapping cables.
    • It has been revealed that finding the best portable SSD is almost a must in the modern tech landscape.
    • It has been revealed that as with any local storage, though, there's a possibility that a drive will suddenly stop working, or fail to run in the first place.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bring a dead external drive back to life with these troubleshooting steps, including Disk Utility and swapping cables.

    It has been revealed that finding the best portable SSD is almost a must in the modern tech landscape. Although you can get by with internal storage and cloud backup, an external drive makes it far easier to move media and document libraries between machines. It can also be a safeguard against worst-case scenarios by starting to use fail safes such as the 3-2-1 rule, which means keeping three copies of your data stored on two types of media with one copy kept in a safe location at home or away from the workplace.

    It has been revealed that as with any local storage, though, there's a possibility that a drive will suddenly stop working, or fail to run in the first place. If these things happen, don't panic, at least not yet. There may be troubleshooting steps you can take to get back on track.

    In a recent development, A few of these should be relatively intuitive, like testing different hardware combinations. Less so are the ones that involve software, since they involve tools you're probably not using on a regular basis, unless perhaps you're an IT professional. Mercifully, if a software fix is possible, you probably won't have to spend any money.

    The first step is to rule out bad hardware that's not your drive. Try plugging it into another port, or swapping in another matching USB or Thunderbolt cable. Thunderbolt cables cover charging, data transfer and video, so it's always good practice to use the right cable and port. Remember also that all external drives require a power supply. Some USB ports on your computer might not have sufficient power, and of course if a drive has a jack for an AC adapter, you're not getting anywhere until that adapter is plugged in. Try plugging a drive into a second computer, if you have one.

    It has been revealed that drives can however be detected by Windows or macOS but still fail to load, possibly because they haven't been formatted correctly. In Windows 11, open Device Manager by searching for it in the taskbar, then expand the Disk drives section. If your drive demonstrates up, you may be able to bring it back by right-clicking on it, then selecting Properties > Volumes > Populate.

    Recent findings suggest that next, click on Disk Management and look for the disk number you should've seen a moment ago. If there's no drive letter assigned, you may be able to assign one. But if the drive is missing NTFS formatting, you may have to reformat it if you want it to work with Windows. You'll lose any existing data on the disk, so treat this option as a last resort. Before reformatting, it's wiser to try Windows' CHKDSK utility. Open the Terminal app using taskbar search, then enter chkdsk [drive letter] /r. This will attempt to both fix errors and recover bad sectors.

    On Macs, the catch-all software solution is typically Disk Utility. Once you've opened the app, select View > Show All Devices. If you see your drive, click on the indented entry and then select Mount at the top of the app. Should that not work, click First Aid instead. This may let you repair errors without losing data. If not, Disk Utility will let you reformat, once again at the cost of wiping a drive clean.

    One simpler possibility is that you need to revision your hardware drivers. This is dead simple on macOS, since Apple typically bundles these in with the latest OS updates. Just head to Apple menu > System Settings > General > Software Update to check. In Windows 11, swing by Settings > Windows Update to install anything there.

    It has been revealed that in some cases, though, Windows consumers may need to return to the right-click Properties menu for a drive in Device Manager. Once you're there, click on the Driver tab, then try updating or uninstalling. If you uninstall without selecting the driver deletion option, restarting your PC should automatically reinstall the correct software, which might repair it.

    Sources indicate that if you've gotten this far without luck, there may not be much you can do other than cross your fingers that a reboot will solve things or seek out third-party help, such as the drive manufacturer or a repair shop. You might need a recovery firm's help if valuable data is trapped. You can also try your Mac or PC's general OS recovery tools, but these are unlikely to fix anything we haven't already suggested.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.

    “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Substantial Tech.”.

    Industry observers note that currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

    Industry observers note that I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

    Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

    Sources indicate that if Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN mentioned. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

    Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

    “Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

    Recent findings suggest that what Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who proposal to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

    “I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon stated. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

    Yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon said. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

    The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

    Other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

    According to recent reports, “It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

    In a recent development, trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

    Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP stated. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

    Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

    In a recent development, “The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth mentioned. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

    “White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth remarked.

    If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.

    In a recent development, detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited New York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

    Industry observers note that also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

    Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

    TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report noted. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

    Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

    Lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

    “In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the organization he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

    After Lutnick was required to hand that firm over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

    Sources indicate that those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.

    Industry observers note that however, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the manufacturer helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

    It has been revealed that among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

    “Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon said.

    Haworth stated the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

    “I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.

    But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

    It seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon said. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal revealed that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

    Recent findings suggest that if US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

    Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon noted could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

    In a recent development, “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon mentioned. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.

    Peter Baker, Paul Sonne and Keith Bradsher reported from Shenzhen, China. Lily Kuo reported from Taipei, Taiwan. Leo Sands reported from London.

    In a recent development, president Trump, Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir V. Putin of Russia greeted each other with smiles and handshakes on Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, hours after Mr. Trump received a personal welcome from Mr. Xi at the Chinese city’s airport that included a hug.

    Sources indicate that the reveals of friendliness by the three world leaders, on the eve of a trilateral summit, contrasted sharply with their divergent stances on some of the world’s most pressing issues, including nuclear arms control, China’s ability to access advanced A.I. chips and the future of the war in Ukraine.

    On Thursday, the presidents are expected to participate in the first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, when at least some of those issues could be on the agenda. The summit will cap Mr. Trump’s whirlwind trip to Asia, which has been shadowed by the Nvidia scandal, trade conflicts and critical infrastructure breakdowns at home.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier, Mr. Xi met Mr. Trump at the airport in Shenzhen, something he did not do when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. But Mr. Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Mr. Xi in September, an uncommon move for an American president and the first time Mr. Trump had done so for a foreign visitor. In effect, Mr. Xi returned the gesture.

    The red-carpet greeting on the tarmac — with a crowd of people in colorful costumes waving flags and flowers and chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin — came shortly after Mr. Xi met with Mr. Putin, who arrived earlier in the day. The Chinese leader had sent a lower-ranking official to greet Mr. Putin but used their subsequent meeting to hail the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the two encounters underscored Mr. Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States. While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have developed a bond, China has a far more extensive economic relationship with the United States.

    Mr. Trump will also meet separately with Mr. Xi on Thursday, his third encounter this year with the Chinese leader after he visited Beijing in the spring and the lavish state visit at the White House a couple months ago. Although Mr. Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent on forging friendly ties between the world’s two largest economies.

    The visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Mr. Trump has remarked he does not intend to raise issues of Chinese interference in American affairs. The chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign last week after revelations of an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence determined was spying for China. But Mr. Trump has said he will not discuss the matter with Mr. Xi.

    Here’s what else we’re covering:.

    It has been revealed that canada: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada mentioned he had met with Mr. Trump on Wednesday in Shenzhen to discuss their countries’ trade dispute. Mr. Carney’s office said that the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement” but offered no further details.

    Recent findings suggest that russian show of force: Russian strategic nuclear bombers landed in Vietnam around when Mr. Putin landed in China, an apparent signal before the trilateral talks with Mr. Trump that Moscow remained the world’s largest nuclear power. Read more ›.

    Fast-food diplomacy: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines said he had fried chicken from Jollibee, a chain that is considered a national treasure, delivered to Mr. Trump during his overnight stay in Manila. Read more ›.

    Sources indicate that president Vladimir V. Putin of Russia held talks for more than two hours with China’s leader, Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before the two leaders were scheduled to meet with President Trump.

    Sources indicate that as Mr. Putin landed in China, Russia engaged in a purposeful show of force by flying strategic nuclear bombers to Vietnam for the first time since the Soviet era. Mr. Putin spent much of the day demonstrating that despite his isolation from many Western nations over their opposition to the war in Ukraine, he remains on good terms with much of the rest of the world.

    In a recent development, mr. Xi greeted Mr. Trump at the airport when the American president arrived in Shenzhen, the first time he has greeted a foreign dignitary on the tarmac in more than a decade as China’s leader. In contrast, Mr. Xi sent a longtime deputy, Cai Qi, to welcome Mr. Putin, who arrived in the early hours of the morning.

    By arriving before Mr. Trump, Mr. Putin got extra face time with Asian leaders ahead of the scheduled trilateral meeting on Thursday between the United States, China and Russia. That meeting will be the first involving the leaders of those three countries.

    Sources indicate that no relationship has proved more critical for Mr. Putin than his bond with Mr. Xi. Mr. Putin met with the Chinese leader for at least the fourth time this year on Wednesday, holding large group talks with the Russian and Chinese delegations in Shenzhen before moving on to a smaller “working breakfast” with top aides.

    In a recent development, as a major purchaser of Russian energy and supplier of electronics and consumer goods, China has served as a lifeline for wartime Russia. Western companies pulled out of the Russian market after the invasion, and Moscow scrambled to adapt in the face of heavy sanctions.

    In a recent development, at the outset of the talks with Mr. Xi, Mr. Putin underscored the rapidly increasing cooperation between Russia and China, noting that tourist flows had increased 43 percent since the countries introduced visa-free travel late last year.

    Mr. Putin stated both Russia and China were taking “constructive approaches to shaping a more equitable, multipolar world order.” That is the Russian leader’s favored oblique terminology for a world no longer dominated by the United States.

    Sources indicate that mr. Putin also met with Vietnam’s leaders before joining a dinner at the summit, where he was welcomed by Mr. Xi and shook Mr. Trump’s hand.

    The scheduled trilateral meeting comes as Moscow continues to play hardball with the Trump administration over talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.

    It has been revealed that mr. Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff last week sought Mr. Putin’s approval to add European officials to talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, but the Kremlin rebuffed the request in public comments after the meeting.

    Recent findings suggest that outside the trilateral meeting, it was not immediately clear how extensive talks between Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin would be. The Kremlin spokesman, Dmitri S. Peskov, told state news media that there most likely would not be time for full-fledged talks between Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin but stated they would find time to discuss Ukraine and possibly Iran.

    Recent findings suggest that at the banquet, President Trump was seated with his back to reporters at the center of the table and Xi Jinping on his left. When reporters were ushered out, the two leaders were conversing through interpreters.

    About an hour later, the president departed and returned to his hotel for the night.

    President Trump, President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia and Xi Jinping, the leader of China, shook hands before the start of a banquet that includes the national leaders of the APEC summit. Trump, Putin and Xi blueprint to hold a trilateral summit on Thursday.

    It has been revealed that xi Jinping, standing at a podium adorned by flowers, lifted a glass of red wine and made a toast at the gathering of leaders. With so many visitors, roads are closed in many places across central Shenzhen.

    Recent findings suggest that amid a bitter trade war between their countries, President Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney met in-person on the sidelines of the APEC summit for the first time since last year. In a statement, Mr. Carney’s office mentioned that the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement” but offered no further details.

    Unlike Trump, Putin was not greeted at the airport by Xi when he arrived in the middle of the night. Cai Qi, Xi’s longtime deputy, met the Russian leader.
